knowledge_statements.title: Necessary Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-subdifferential Fermat certificate for a constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, and set \(F=f+\delta_C\). If \(\bar x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\), then the limiting Fermat condition is \[0\in\partial F(\bar x).\] Whenever the exact sum rule \(\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\) is valid, this yields the decomposed certificate \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x).\] The inclusion is necessary under these assumptions; absent additional structure, it does not certify local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained local minimizer must be stationary for the objective plus the constraint indicator; an exact sum rule separates this into subgradient and normal components.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x)\), with \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\) under the exact sum rule.

notation.meaning: Indicator of the feasible set: zero on C and positive infinity outside C.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity for a nonsmooth constrained problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity is defined by the previously stated normalized multiplier condition, equivalently by membership of zero in the stationarity mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(\bar x\in S\) is stationary for \(f\) on \(S\) if it satisfies condition \((2.65)\), equivalently if \(0\in\widetilde M(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is stationary when it satisfies the normalized multiplier necessary condition, equivalently when zero belongs to the stationarity mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ is stationary for }f\text{ on }S\iff 0\in\widetilde M(\bar x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary Directional Condition for a Constrained Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary first-order condition for minimizing a subdifferentiable function over a set, using the source-defined direction family \(\Gamma(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the subdifferentiable function \(f\) attains its smallest value on \(\Omega\) at \(x^*\in\Omega\), then \[\max_{v\in\partial f(x^*)}\langle v,g\rangle\geq 0\qquad\forall g\in\Gamma(x^*).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a subdifferentiable function attains its minimum over Omega at x*, then its maximum subgradient pairing is nonnegative for every direction in the source-defined family Gamma(x*).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{v\in\partial f(x^*)}\langle v,g\rangle\geq 0\quad\forall g\in\Gamma(x^*)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian stationarity and abstract maximum principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A locally Lipschitz nonsmooth multiplier condition, with a supporting-functional conclusion for a convex set constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a local solution. Suppose that \(X\) is Asplund, every \(\varphi_i\), \(0\le i\le m+r\), is locally Lipschitz around \(\bar x\), and \(\Omega\) is locally closed around \(\bar x\). Then there are multipliers \(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{m+r}\), not all zero, such that \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for \(0\le i\le m\), \(\lambda_i\varphi_i(\bar x)=0\) for \(1\le i\le m\), and \[0\in\partial L(\cdot,\lambda)(\bar x)+N(\bar x;\Omega).\] If \(\Omega\) is additionally convex, then for some \(x^*\in-\partial L(\cdot,\lambda)(\bar x)\), \[\langle x^*,\bar x\rangle=\max\{\langle x^*,x\rangle:x\in\Omega\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz constrained local minimizer in an Asplund space satisfies a nontrivial nonsmooth Lagrangian stationarity condition with multiplier signs and complementary slackness. If the set constraint is convex, an opposing Lagrangian subgradient supports that set at the minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \varphi_i\text{ is locally Lipschitz around }\bar x\quad(0\le i\le m+r)
\Omega\text{ is convex only for the maximum-principle conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda\ne0:\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ \lambda_i\varphi_i(\bar x)=0,\ 0\in\partial L(\cdot,\lambda)(\bar x)+N(\bar x;\Omega);\quad \Omega\text{ convex}\Rightarrow\exists x^*\in-\partial L(\cdot,\lambda)(\bar x):\ \langle x^*,\bar x\rangle=\max_{x\in\Omega}\langle x^*,x\rangle.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of an unconstrained stationary point; the necessary-optimality assertion is understood under the surrounding locally Lipschitz assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^N\) is stationary for \(f\) if \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Under the surrounding locally Lipschitz assumptions, local optimality implies stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is stationary when zero belongs to its subdifferential. In the stated locally Lipschitz setting, stationarity is necessary for local optimality.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is locally Lipschitz for the necessary-optimality assertion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ is stationary for }f\iff 0\in\partial f(\bar x),\qquad \bar x\text{ locally minimizing}\implies 0\in\partial f(\bar x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary multipliers for programs with many geometric constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order generalized-differential necessary conditions for nonsmooth mathematical programs with multiple geometric constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar z\) be a local optimal solution of (6.29). Suppose \(Z\) and \(E\) are Asplund spaces, each \(\Xi_j\) is locally closed and SNC at \(\bar z\), each \(\varphi_i\) is Lipschitz continuous near \(\bar z\), and \(f\) is generalized Fredholm at \(\bar z\). Then there exist \(\mu_j\in\mathbb R\) for \(j=0,\ldots,s\), \(e^*\in E^*\), and \(z_j^*\in Z^*\) for \(j=1,\ldots,l\), not all zero, such that \(\mu_j\ge0\) for \(j=0,\ldots,s\), \(\mu_j\varphi_j(\bar z)=0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,s\), \(z_j^*\in N(\bar z;\Xi_j)\), and \(-\sum_{j=1}^l z_j^*\in\partial(\sum_{j=0}^s\mu_j\varphi_j)(\bar z)+D_N^*f(\bar z)(e^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated Asplund-space, local-closedness, SNC, Lipschitz, and generalized-Fredholm assumptions, a local optimum admits nontrivial scalar and dual multipliers satisfying sign, complementarity, normal-cone, and generalized stationarity conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar z\) is a local optimal solution of problem (6.29).
Every \(\Xi_j\) is locally closed and SNC at \(\bar z\).
Every \(\varphi_i\) is Lipschitz continuous near \(\bar z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(\mu_0,\ldots,\mu_s,e^*,z_1^*,\ldots,z_l^*\), not all zero, satisfying \(\mu_j\ge0\), complementarity, \(z_j^*\in N(\bar z;\Xi_j)\), and \(-\sum_{j=1}^l z_j^*\in\partial(\sum_{j=0}^s\mu_j\varphi_j)(\bar z)+D_N^*f(\bar z)(e^*)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contingent-Cone Necessary Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order necessary stationarity for differentiable minimization over an arbitrary set, expressed through the negative polar of its contingent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset\mathbf{E}\) and \(x\in S\). If \(x\) is a local minimizer of the real-valued function \(f\) on \(S\) and \(f\) is Fréchet differentiable at \(x\), then \[-\nabla f(x)\in K_S(x)^-.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimum over a set, the negative gradient of a Fréchet-differentiable objective belongs to the negative polar of the set's contingent cone.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is a local minimizer of }f\text{ on }S
f\text{ is real-valued and Fréchet differentiable at }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\nabla f(x)\in K_S(x)^-

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsmooth KKT Necessary Conditions under the Cottle Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order necessary conditions for the locally Lipschitz inequality-constrained problem (4.11).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x^*\in S\neq\varnothing\) is a local optimum of problem (4.11), \(f,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are locally Lipschitz at \(x^*\), and the Cottle constraint qualification holds at \(x^*\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local optimum of problem (4.11) satisfying the Cottle constraint qualification and the stated local Lipschitz assumptions admits nonnegative multipliers satisfying complementarity and nonsmooth KKT stationarity.

f,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ are locally Lipschitz at }x^*

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary conditions via separate epigraph and graph normals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate, limiting-normal, and Lipschitz subgradient certificates for a local solution of a functionally constrained problem in an Asplund space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be Asplund, let \(\bar x\) be a local solution of the functional-constraint problem, and let \(\Omega\) be locally closed around \(\bar x\). (i) If \(\varphi_i\) is lower semicontinuous around \(\bar x\) for \(0\le i\le m\) and continuous there for \(m+1\le i\le m+r\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there are nearby points on the corresponding epigraphs, graphs, and \(\Omega\), and \(\varepsilon\)-approximate Fréchet normals \((x_i^*,-\lambda_i)\) and \(\widehat x^*\), such that \(\sum_{i=0}^{m+r}x_i^*+\widehat x^*=0\) and \(\sum_{i=0}^{m+r}\|(x_i^*,\lambda_i)\|+\|\widehat x^*\|=1\). (ii) If all but one of those epigraphs, graphs, and \(\Omega\) are SNC at their reference points, an exact normalized limiting-normal certificate exists with \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for \(0\le i\le m\). If each inactive inequality function is upper semicontinuous at \(\bar x\), then \(\lambda_i\varphi_i(\bar x)=0\) for \(1\le i\le m\). (iii) If every \(\varphi_i\) is locally Lipschitz around \(\bar x\), there is a nonzero multiplier vector satisfying \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for all \(i\), complementary slackness for the inequalities, and \[0\in\sum_{i=0}^{m}\lambda_i\partial\varphi_i(\bar x)+\sum_{i=m+1}^{m+r}\lambda_i\bigl[\partial\varphi_i(\bar x)\cup\partial(-\varphi_i)(\bar x)\bigr]+N(\bar x;\Omega).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local solution admits normalized approximate Fréchet-normal certificates at nearby epigraph and graph points. SNC gives an exact limiting-normal certificate, while local Lipschitz continuity gives a nontrivial subgradient multiplier condition with the stated signs and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \text{The lower-semicontinuity, continuity, SNC, upper-semicontinuity, and Lipschitz hypotheses apply only in their stated branches.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The three branches yield, respectively, an approximate Fréchet-normal balance, an exact normalized limiting-normal balance, and a nonzero limiting-subgradient multiplier inclusion.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SB-KKT Conditions as Necessary Optimality Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bilevel-specific necessary stationarity certificate for the cited ℓp-regularized reformulation; the source states the constraint qualification only as “appropriate.”
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<p\leq 1\), and let \((w^*,\lambda^*)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\) be a local optimum of problem (6.3.4). Suppose an appropriate constraint qualification holds for the constraints \[\frac{\partial G(w,\bar\lambda)}{\partial w_i}+p\operatorname{sgn}(w_i)\lambda_1|w_i|^{p-1}=0\quad(i\notin I(w^*)),\qquad w_i=0\quad(i\in I(w^*)),\qquad \lambda\geq0.\] Then there exist \(\zeta^*\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\eta^*\in\mathbb R^r\) such that \((w^*,\lambda^*)\), together with \((\zeta^*,\eta^*)\), satisfies the SB-KKT conditions (6.3.5)–(6.3.10).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an appropriate constraint qualification, every local optimum of the specified ℓp-regularized bilevel reformulation admits adjoint and multiplier vectors satisfying the SB-KKT system.
assumptions_latex: (w^*,\lambda^*)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\text{ is a local optimum of problem (6.3.4)}
\text{An appropriate constraint qualification holds for the displayed constraints}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\zeta^*\in\mathbb R^n,\ \exists\eta^*\in\mathbb R^r:\ (w^*,\lambda^*,\zeta^*,\eta^*)\text{ satisfies (6.3.5)--(6.3.10).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fritz John multipliers and normalization for Lipschitzian programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded nonsmooth necessary conditions for a feasible local minimizer of the Lipschitzian program under consideration. The additional active-subgradient condition is required only for normalization of the objective multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a feasible solution of the Lipschitzian programming problem under consideration and a local minimizer of \(\varphi_0\). Then there exist multipliers \(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_m\ge 0\), not all zero, such that \(\lambda_i\varphi_i(\bar x)=0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(0\in\sum_{i=0}^m\lambda_i\partial\varphi_i(\bar x)\). Define \(I(\bar x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:\varphi_i(\bar x)=0\}\). If, for every selection \(v_i\in\partial\varphi_i(\bar x)\), \(i\in I(\bar x)\), the implication \(\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\mu_i v_i=0,\ \mu_i\ge0\Rightarrow\mu_i=0\ \forall i\in I(\bar x)\) holds, then these necessary conditions hold with \(\lambda_0=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible local minimizer of the Lipschitzian program admits nonnegative, nontrivial Fritz John multipliers satisfying complementary slackness and a subdifferential Lagrangian inclusion. If every selected family of active-constraint subgradients is positively linearly independent, the objective multiplier can be normalized to one.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\text{ is feasible for the Lipschitzian programming problem and locally minimizes }\varphi_0.
\text{For normalization only: }\forall v_i\in\partial\varphi_i(\bar x),\quad \left[\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\mu_i v_i=0,\ \mu_i\ge0\right]\Rightarrow\left[\mu_i=0\ \forall i\in I(\bar x)\right].
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_m)\in\mathbb{R}_+^{m+1}\setminus\{0\}:\quad \lambda_i\varphi_i(\bar x)=0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad 0\in\sum_{i=0}^m\lambda_i\partial\varphi_i(\bar x);\quad \text{under the additional condition, the multipliers may be chosen with }\lambda_0=1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extended Lagrange principle for nonsmooth functional constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A necessary multiplier certificate expressed through a generalized-epigraph normal, a normal coderivative, and, under relative Lipschitz continuity, the essential Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be Asplund and let \(\bar x\) be a local solution. Assume that \(\Omega\) is locally closed around \(\bar x\), that \(\varphi_i\) is lower semicontinuous around \(\bar x\) relative to \(\Omega\) for \(0\le i\le m\), and that \(\varphi_i\) is continuous there relative to \(\Omega\) for \(m+1\le i\le m+r\). Then there is a multiplier vector \(\lambda\ne0\) such that \[(0,-\lambda_0,\ldots,-\lambda_{m+r})\in N\bigl((\bar x,0);\mathcal E(\varphi_0,\ldots,\varphi_{m+r},\Omega)\bigr).\] This implies \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for \(0\le i\le m\) and \(\lambda_i\varphi_i(\bar x)=0\) for \(1\le i\le m\). Under the stated additional relative-continuity condition for the equality functions, it also implies \[0\in D_N^*\bigl((\varphi_0,\ldots,\varphi_{m+r})+\Delta(\cdot;\Omega)\bigr)(\bar x)(\lambda).\] If every \(\varphi_i\) is locally Lipschitz around \(\bar x\) relative to \(\Omega\), this coderivative inclusion is equivalent to \(0\in\partial L_\Omega(\cdot,\lambda)(\bar x)\), and the generalized-epigraph normal condition is equivalent to this essential-Lagrangian stationarity together with sign and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local solution has a nonzero multiplier represented by a normal to the generalized constraint epigraph. This yields sign and complementary-slackness conditions and a normal-coderivative condition; relative local Lipschitz continuity makes the latter equivalent to essential-Lagrangian stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \varphi_i\text{ is lower semicontinuous relative to }\Omega\text{ for }0\le i\le m
\varphi_i\text{ is continuous relative to }\Omega\text{ for }m+1\le i\le m+r
\text{Equivalence with essential-Lagrangian stationarity requires every }\varphi_i\text{ to be locally Lipschitz relative to }\Omega.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda\ne0:\ (0,-\lambda)\in N((\bar x,0);\mathcal E),\quad \lambda_i\ge0,\quad\lambda_i\varphi_i(\bar x)=0;\quad\text{the stated stronger hypotheses yield coderivative and essential-Lagrangian forms.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak fuzzy stationarity for non-Lipschitz constrained problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate Fréchet-subdifferential necessary conditions for local minimizers with inequality, equality, and set constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer of \(\min\{\varphi_0(x):\varphi_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ \varphi_i(x)=0\ (i=m+1,\ldots,m+r),\ x\in\Omega\}\) in an Asplund space. For each equality constraint, the selected covector may come from the function or its negative.

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex first-order certificate for global, hence local, optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Suppose \(\bar x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) and the convex subdifferential sum rule applies at \(\bar x\). Then \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\] holds if and only if \[f(\bar x)\le f(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in C.\] Thus a displayed pair \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\) and \(-v\in N_C(\bar x)\) is a verifiable sufficient certificate of global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective and convex feasible set, balancing an objective subgradient with a feasible-set normal is equivalent to global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The convex subdifferential sum rule holds at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\iff \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of f at the candidate point.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Stationarity Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and neighborhood measures derived from limiting subdifferential stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=f+\delta_C\) and \(x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), define the pointwise stationarity residual by \[r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))=\inf\{\lVert v\rVert:v\in\partial F(x)\},\] with \(r(x)=+\infty\) when \(\partial F(x)=\varnothing\). The point \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-stationary when \(r(x)\le\varepsilon\). For \(\rho>0\), define the neighborhood residual \[r_\rho(x)=\inf\{r(y):y\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f,\ \lVert y-x\rVert\le\rho\}.\] Reporting \((\rho,\varepsilon)\) with \(r_\rho(x)\le\varepsilon\) certifies the existence of an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary point within distance \(\rho\) of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity can be quantified by distance from zero to the subdifferential, either at the reported point or at some point in a prescribed neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(x)\le\varepsilon\) defines pointwise approximate stationarity, while \(r_\rho(x)\le\varepsilon\) defines neighborhood approximate stationarity.

notation.meaning: Best stationarity residual within radius rho.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Derivative Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible lower-Hadamard directional condition required at a constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(\bar x\in C\). For \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\), define the feasible lower-Hadamard derivative by \[d^-_C f(\bar x;d)=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0,\ d'\to d\\ \bar x+td'\in C}}\frac{f(\bar x+td')-f(\bar x)}{t}.\] If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\), then \[d^-_C f(\bar x;d)\ge0\quad\text{for every }d\in T_C(\bar x).\] A direction with strictly negative derivative therefore certifies failure of local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible tangent direction at a local minimizer has nonnegative feasible lower directional derivative; a negative direction disproves local optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) relative to \(C\).
The feasible lower-Hadamard derivative is interpreted through feasible perturbation sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^-_C f(\bar x;d)\ge0\) for every \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Cone Feasible Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential definition of first-order feasible directions for an arbitrary set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and a point \(\bar x\in C\), the Bouligand tangent cone is \[T_C(\bar x)=\left\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists\,t_k\downarrow0,\ \exists\,x_k\in C,\ x_k\to\bar x,\ \frac{x_k-\bar x}{t_k}\to d\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\) exactly when there exist \(t_k\downarrow0\) and \(d_k\to d\) such that \(\bar x+t_kd_k\in C\) for every \(k\). These are the directions attainable to first order by feasible sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bouligand tangent cone contains precisely the limits of scaled feasible displacements approaching the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(\bar x)\) is the set of sequentially attainable first-order feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional–Tangent Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex regime equating tangent-direction tests, subgradient-normal balance, and optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite and convex, let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(\bar x\in C\). Then the following statements are equivalent: \[f'(\bar x;d)\ge0\quad\text{for every }d\in T_C(\bar x),\] \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x),\] and \[f(\bar x)=\min_{x\in C}f(x).\] Thus, in this convex finite-valued regime, the primal directional certificate on the tangent cone and the dual subgradient-normal certificate represent the same optimality condition. Outside regular convex regimes, this equivalence need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite convex objective on a closed convex set, nonnegative derivatives on the tangent cone, subgradient-normal stationarity, and global optimality are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(\bar x;d)\ge0\ \forall d\in T_C(\bar x)\iff0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\iff\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential Stationarity Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite limiting-subdifferential condition for constrained nonsmooth stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, and define \(F=f+\delta_C\). A feasible point \(\bar x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) is limiting-subdifferential stationary when \[0\in\partial F(\bar x).\] Equivalently, the stationarity residual \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(\bar x))\) vanishes. If an exact subdifferential sum rule is available, the condition can be checked through vectors \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\) and \(n\in N_C(\bar x)\) satisfying \(v+n=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is limiting-subdifferential stationary when zero belongs to the subdifferential of the objective plus the feasible-set indicator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Stationarity Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-balance formulation of constrained first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed. A feasible point \(\bar x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) satisfies the subgradient-normal stationarity condition when there exists \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\) such that \[-v\in N_C(\bar x).\] Equivalently, \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x).\] A pair \((v,-v)\) supplies explicit primal-objective and constraint-normal components whose sum is zero. The condition agrees with composite stationarity only in regimes where the relevant subdifferential sum rule is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal-cone stationarity requires an objective subgradient to be canceled by a normal to the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists v\in\partial f(\bar x)\) such that \(-v\in N_C(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient–Normal Translation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex qualification ensuring exact translation between composite and decomposed stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. If \[\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}C\ne\varnothing,\] then for every \(x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), \[\partial(f+\delta_C)(x)=\partial f(x)+N_C(x).\] Consequently, composite stationarity, decomposed stationarity, and subgradient-normal balance are equivalent: \[0\in\partial(f+\delta_C)(x)\iff0\in\partial f(x)+N_C(x)\iff\exists v\in\partial f(x): -v\in N_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex relative-interior qualification makes the indicator sum rule exact, translating composite stationarity into an objective-subgradient and feasible-normal balance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(f+\delta_C)(x)=\partial f(x)+N_C(x)\) for every \(x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-System Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT multiplier representation for smooth inequality-constrained programs under MFCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)\le0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\] where \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are continuously differentiable near a feasible local minimizer \(\bar x\). If the Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification holds at \(\bar x\), then there is \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying \[\nabla f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x)=0,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0.\] Together with primal feasibility, this multiplier system represents first-order stationarity and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, a smooth constrained local minimizer admits nonnegative multipliers satisfying Lagrangian stationarity and complementary slackness.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is a feasible local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\lambda\ge0\) satisfying Lagrangian stationarity and \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\) for all \(i\).

notation.meaning: Gradient of the Lagrangian with respect to the decision variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Equation Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued generalized equation encoding of constrained stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable and let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed. The normal-cone stationarity condition for minimizing \(f\) over \(C\) is the generalized equation \[0\in\nabla f(x)+N_C(x).\] More generally, for a single-valued mapping \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times P\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and a set-valued mapping \(Q:\mathbb{R}^n\times P\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\), the parameterized stationary solution map is \[S(p)=\{x:0\in F(x,p)+Q(x,p)\}.\] Choosing \(F=\nabla f\) and \(Q=N_C\) recovers the constrained first-order certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained stationarity is a generalized equation whose single-valued term is the objective gradient and whose set-valued term is the feasible-set normal cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is normal-stationary exactly when \(0\in\nabla f(x)+N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Set-valued term of a generalized equation.

children.title: Multiplier–Equation Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier–Equation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between inequality multipliers and a cone-valued generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For continuously differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), a pair \((x,\lambda)\) satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementary slackness, and Lagrangian stationarity precisely when \[0=\nabla f(x)+\nabla g(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda,\qquad 0\in-g(x)+N_{\mathbb{R}_+^m}(\lambda).\] Indeed, the second generalized equation is equivalent componentwise to \[g_i(x)\le0,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(x)=0.\] Thus the multiplier system and the generalized-equation representation have exactly the same solution pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth inequalities, feasibility and complementarity are equivalent to one normal-cone generalized equation, while its companion equation gives Lagrangian stationarity.
assumptions_latex: The feasible inequalities use the convention \(g(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT system is equivalent to \(0=\nabla f(x)+\nabla g(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) and \(0\in-g(x)+N_{\mathbb{R}_+^m}(\lambda)\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative orthant for the multiplier vector.
Convex normal cone to the nonnegative orthant at lambda.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Subdifferential regularity at \(\bar x\) means that the regular and limiting subdifferentials coincide there. Thus \[\widehat\partial f(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar x).\] If \(f\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), regularity also yields equality with the Clarke subdifferential: \[\widehat\partial f(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar x)=\partial_C f(\bar x).\] Hence the corresponding zero-inclusion stationarity certificates are equivalent at \(\bar x\). Proper lower semicontinuous convex functions furnish a principal coincidence regime at every point of their domains.

children.title: Strict Hierarchy Separations
children.top_down_role: Examples and regimes where adjacent stationarity notions remain genuinely distinct.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial f_1(0)\setminus\widehat\partial f_1(0)\) and \(0\in\partial_C f_2(0)\setminus\partial f_2(0)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: subdifferentials of elementary one-dimensional piecewise-linear functions are directly calculable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete one-dimensional separations of consecutive regular, limiting, and Clarke stationarity classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_1(x)=\min\{x,0\}\), direct calculation gives \[\widehat\partial f_1(0)=\varnothing,\qquad \partial f_1(0)=\{0,1\},\qquad \partial_C f_1(0)=[0,1].\] Thus \(0\) is limiting-stationary but not regular-stationary. For \(f_2(x)=-|x|\), \[\widehat\partial f_2(0)=\varnothing,\qquad \partial f_2(0)=\{-1,1\},\qquad \partial_C f_2(0)=[-1,1].\] Thus \(0\) is Clarke-stationary but not limiting-stationary. Both inclusions in the stationarity hierarchy are therefore strict over locally Lipschitz functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two elementary piecewise-linear functions show that limiting stationarity can exceed regular stationarity and Clarke stationarity can exceed limiting stationarity.

children.title: Failed Reverse Implications
children.top_down_role: Boundaries preventing converse passage along stationarity implication routes.

assumptions_latex: Stationarity notions are defined by zero membership in the Fréchet, limiting, and Clarke subdifferentials.
The objectives are finite-valued and locally Lipschitz on \(\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial_C f(0)\not\Rightarrow0\in\partial f(0)\) and \(0\in\partial g(0)\not\Rightarrow0\in\widehat\partial g(0)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary counterexamples disprove the reverse implications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the reverse arrows without subdifferential regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reverse implication from Clarke to limiting stationarity fails for \(f(x)=-|x|\), since \[0\in\partial_C f(0)=[-1,1],\qquad 0\notin\partial f(0)=\{-1,1\}.\] The reverse implication from limiting to regular stationarity fails for \(g(x)=\min\{x,0\}\), since \[0\in\partial g(0)=\{0,1\},\qquad \widehat\partial g(0)=\varnothing.\] Therefore local Lipschitz continuity alone does not reverse either implication in the regular-to-limiting-to-Clarke hierarchy.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Subdifferential Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global optimality characterization for proper convex functions in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convex subdifferential is \[\partial f(\bar x)=\left\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\geq f(\bar x)+\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\text{ for all }x\in\mathbb{R}^n\right\}.\] For a proper lower semicontinuous convex function, \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x)\geq f(\bar x)\text{ for all }x\in\mathbb{R}^n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f.\] Thus convex subdifferential stationarity is both necessary and sufficient for global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower semicontinuous convex function, zero belongs to the convex subdifferential exactly at global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\Longleftrightarrow0\in\partial f(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fréchet-Subgradient Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional definition through first-order lower approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Fréchet subdifferential of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) is \[\widehat\partial f(\bar x)=\left\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\liminf_{\substack{x\to\bar x\\x\neq\bar x}}\frac{f(x)-f(\bar x)-\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle}{\|x-\bar x\|}\geq0\right\}.\] The point \(\bar x\) is Fréchet-subgradient stationary when \(0\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\), equivalently when \[\liminf_{\substack{x\to\bar x\\x\neq\bar x}}\frac{f(x)-f(\bar x)}{\|x-\bar x\|}\geq0.\] Every local minimizer at which \(f\) is finite satisfies this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fréchet stationarity means that zero gives a first-order lower affine approximation to the objective at the point.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is Fréchet-subgradient stationary exactly when \(0\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In finite-dimensional variational analysis, the regular subdifferential is the Fréchet subdifferential: \[\partial^{\mathrm{reg}}f(\bar x):=\widehat\partial f(\bar x).\] Accordingly, regular-subgradient stationarity is the condition \[0\in\partial^{\mathrm{reg}}f(\bar x),\] which is identical to Fréchet-subgradient stationarity. If \(f\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), then \(\widehat\partial f(\bar x)=\{\nabla f(\bar x)\}\), so regular stationarity reduces to the smooth Fermat equation \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular subgradient and Fréchet subgradient are two names for the same object, so their stationarity conditions coincide.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a subdifferentially regular point \(\bar x\), \[\widehat\partial f(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar x).\] Therefore \[0\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\partial f(\bar x).\] This coincidence holds, in particular, for proper lower semicontinuous convex functions at points of their domains and for continuously differentiable functions, where both subdifferentials reduce to the convex subdifferential or the gradient singleton, respectively. The equality is pointwise and need not persist at nearby nonregular points.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is Mordukhovich critical, or limiting critical, for the unconstrained problem \(\min_x f(x)\) when \[0\in\partial f(\bar x),\] where \(\partial f(\bar x)\) is the limiting subdifferential. This is precisely limiting-subgradient stationarity. Since \(\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\subseteq\partial f(\bar x)\), every regular-stationary point is Mordukhovich critical. The converse can fail unless subdifferential regularity makes the regular and limiting subdifferentials coincide.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed-graph stability for the limiting subdifferential under function-value convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The limiting subdifferential has a sequentially closed graph relative to function-value convergence: if \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\), \(v_k\to v\), and \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) for every \(k\), then \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Thus limits of exact limiting-subgradient stationarity certificates remain valid when both the iterates and their objective values converge appropriately. In particular, if \(v_k=0\) for every \(k\), then \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limiting subgradients pass to convergent limits when the points, function values, and subgradients converge; consequently, limiting stationarity is stable in this regime.

children.top_down_role: Irregular settings where limiting certificates do not recover regular stationarity.

assumptions_latex: \(\widehat\partial f\) and \(\partial f\) denote the regular and limiting subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial f(0)\) need not imply \(0\in\widehat\partial f(0)\), although \(\widehat\partial f(0)\subseteq\partial f(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation between regular and limiting stationarity in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Always \(\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\subseteq\partial f(\bar x)\), so regular stationarity implies limiting stationarity, but the converse can fail. Define \(f(0)=0\) and, for \(x\ne0\), \(f(x)=-|x|+x^2\sin(1/|x|)\). At \(0\), incompatible one-sided slopes give \(\widehat\partial f(0)=\varnothing\). For \(x_k=((2k+1)\pi)^{-1}>0\), the function is differentiable and \(f'(x_k)=0\); hence the gradient-limit construction yields \(0\in\partial f(0)\). Therefore limiting stationarity does not certify regular stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular stationarity always implies limiting stationarity, but a locally Lipschitz oscillatory cusp can be limiting-stationary while having no regular subgradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation from Regular Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_f\) be the set where \(f\) is differentiable. Its Clarke generalized gradient is \[\partial^{\mathrm C}f(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\left\{v:\exists x_k\in D_f,\ x_k\to\bar x,\ \nabla f(x_k)\to v\right\}.\] The point \(\bar x\) is Clarke-stationary if and only if \(0\in\partial^{\mathrm C}f(\bar x)\). Equivalently, zero belongs to the convex hull of all gradients attainable as limits along differentiability points approaching \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz objective is Clarke-stationary when zero lies in the convex hull of gradients limiting from nearby differentiability points.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every unconstrained local minimizer of a locally Lipschitz function is Clarke-stationary. For a finite convex function, Clarke stationarity is equivalent to global unconstrained optimality.

g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ is convex, for the global equivalence}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the reachable-gradient set by \[G_f(\bar x)=\left\{v:\exists x_k\in D_f,\ x_k\to\bar x,\ \nabla f(x_k)\to v\right\}.\] The point \(\bar x\) is gradient-limit stationary when \(0\in G_f(\bar x)\); equivalently, there are differentiability points \(x_k\to\bar x\) for which \(\nabla f(x_k)\to0\). Since \(G_f(\bar x)\subseteq\operatorname{co}G_f(\bar x)=\partial^{\mathrm C}f(\bar x)\), this condition implies Clarke stationarity and may be strictly stronger.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient-limit stationarity requires gradients at nearby differentiability points to converge to zero, without taking convex combinations of distinct limiting gradients.

children.title: Proximal Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Criticality based on proximal subgradients or local quadratic support.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial_P f(\bar x)\) exactly when \(f(x)\ge f(\bar x)-\frac r2\|x-\bar x\|^2\) locally for some \(r\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Proximal subdifferential of f at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional proximal-subgradient stationarity expressed by local quadratic support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(v\) is a proximal subgradient of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) when there exist \(r\ge0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \[f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle-\frac r2\|x-\bar x\|^2\qquad(x\in U).\] Proximal stationarity is the certificate \(0\in\partial_P f(\bar x)\). It is therefore verifiable by exhibiting \(r\ge0\) and \(U\) for which \(f(x)\ge f(\bar x)-\frac r2\|x-\bar x\|^2\) throughout \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal stationarity means the objective has a local downward quadratic support at the point with zero linear term.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define the lower Dini directional derivative by \[f'_D(\bar x;d)=\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{f(\bar x+td)-f(\bar x)}{t}.\] The point \(\bar x\) is Dini-stationary when \(f'_D(\bar x;d)\ge0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary stationarity implications for locally Lipschitz unconstrained minimization, including failure of the converse from Clarke to Dini stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be locally Lipschitz near a local minimizer \(x^*\). Then \(x^*\) is Dini stationary. If \(f\) is also directionally differentiable at \(x^*\), then \(f'(x^*;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\), so \(x^*\) is directionally stationary. In general, Dini stationarity implies Clarke stationarity, but Clarke stationarity need not imply Dini stationarity.

The point \(\bar x\) is directionally stationary, or d-stationary, if \(f'(\bar x;d)\ge0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\). This condition excludes every first-order feasible descent direction; for an unconstrained local minimizer at which all these derivatives exist, it is necessary.

children.title: DC Critical Points
children.top_down_role: Criticality tied to a selected difference-of-convex representation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is DC-critical exactly when \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-relative DC criticality for finite convex component functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the DC representation \(f=g-h\). A point \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is DC-critical for this representation when there exists \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \[v\in\partial g(\bar x)\quad\text{and}\quad v\in\partial h(\bar x).\] Equivalently, \(\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\), or \(0\in\partial g(\bar x)-\partial h(\bar x)\). The certificate consists of the point and a common convex subgradient of the two selected DC components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is critical for a chosen DC decomposition when the two convex components possess a common subgradient there.
knowledge_statements.title: DC Critical Points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common-subgradient condition is a standard representation-relative DC criticality convention and fits the condition container, but no source establishes that convention here.

children.title: Strong DC Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Stronger DC certificates retaining directional information.

assumptions_latex: Both convex directional derivatives are taken at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g'(\bar x;d)-h'(\bar x;d)\ge0\) for every \(d\), equivalently \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Directional derivative of the DC objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional strong stationarity for a fixed finite-valued DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(\bar x\) is strongly DC-stationary for the decomposition \(f=g-h\) when \[f'(\bar x;d)=g'(\bar x;d)-h'(\bar x;d)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Because finite convex functions satisfy \(g'(\bar x;d)=\max_{u\in\partial g(\bar x)}\langle u,d\rangle\) and analogously for \(h\), this condition is equivalent to \(\partial h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial g(\bar x)\). It implies ordinary DC criticality whenever \(\partial h(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong DC stationarity requires every directional derivative of the chosen DC difference to be nonnegative, equivalently inclusion of the component subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong DC Stationarity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For finite convex components, the directional inequality and subdifferential inclusion are consistent. The name and exact strength of strong DC stationarity vary across sources and therefore require an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.title: DC Decomposition Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete one-dimensional failure of decomposition invariance for DC criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x\). The decomposition \(g_1(x)=x\), \(h_1(x)=0\) gives \(\partial g_1(0)=\{1\}\) and \(\partial h_1(0)=\{0\}\), so \(0\) is not DC-critical. The equally valid decomposition \(g_2(x)=x+|x|\), \(h_2(x)=|x|\) gives \(\partial g_2(0)=[0,2]\) and \(\partial h_2(0)=[-1,1]\), whose intersection is \([0,1]\). Hence \(0\) is DC-critical for the second representation although the represented objective is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the same linear function, one DC decomposition makes zero noncritical while adding the same absolute-value term to both components makes it critical.
assumptions_latex: The same function \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) is represented by two pairs of finite convex functions.
DC criticality is tested by intersection of the selected component subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: DC criticality can change when the decomposition changes, even though \(f\) is unchanged.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \(\bar x\) is active-piece stationary for \(f\) if there are coefficients \(\lambda_i\ge 0\), indexed by \(i\in I(\bar x)\), such that \(\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\lambda_i=1\) and
\[
\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\lambda_i\nabla f_i(\bar x)=0.
\]
Equivalently, the zero vector belongs to the convex hull of the gradients of precisely those pieces attaining the maximum at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-piece stationarity holds when a convex combination of the gradients of the pieces attaining the maximum equals zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The pair \((A,B)\) is a directional saddle-point stationarity certificate at \(\bar x\) when
\[
-B\subseteq A.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional saddle point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional first-order saddle concept for a bifunction on a constrained product set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $L:\mathcal O_x\times\mathcal O_y\to\mathbb R$. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimax characterization and existence of directional saddle points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of directional saddle points through directional stationarity and equality of derivative minimax values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $X\times Y\subset\mathbb R^{n+m}$ be compact and convex, and let $L$ satisfy (L1)--(L3) and (L4) at a given $\bar x\in X$. Then $(\bar x,\bar y)$ is a d-saddle point on $X\times Y$ if and only if $\bar x$ is a d-stationary solution of (6.14), $\bar y\in M(\bar x)$, and
\[\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in M(\bar x)}L(\cdot,y)'(\bar x;x-\bar x)=\max_{y\in M(\bar x)}\min_{x\in X}L(\cdot,y)'(\bar x;x-\bar x)=\min_{x\in X}L(\cdot,\bar y)'(\bar x;x-\bar x).\]
If $(\bar x,\bar y)$ is a d-saddle point, all three values equal zero. Moreover, $L$ has a d-saddle point on $X\times Y$ if and only if (6.14) has a d-stationary solution $\bar x$ satisfying
\[\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in M(\bar x)}L(\cdot,y)'(\bar x;x-\bar x)=\max_{y\in M(\bar x)}\min_{x\in X}L(\cdot,y)'(\bar x;x-\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact convex product set and under assumptions L1–L4, a pair is a directional saddle point exactly when its first component is a directionally stationary solution of the referenced problem, its second component lies in the response set, and the derivative min–max, max–min, and selected-response minimum agree. For a directional saddle point these values are zero. Existence is equivalent to a directionally stationary solution satisfying the derivative min–max equality.
assumptions_latex: X\times Y\subset\mathbb R^{n+m}\text{ is compact and convex}
L\text{ satisfies (L4) at a given }\bar x\in X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a d-saddle point iff the stated stationarity, response-set, and three-value equalities hold; for a d-saddle point the three values are zero. Existence is equivalent to a d-stationary }\bar x\text{ satisfying the derivative minimax equality.}

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, with \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial_{\varepsilon}f(\bar x)\), equivalently \(f(\bar x)\le\inf f+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex epsilon-subdifferential; this pointwise condition is equivalent to epsilon-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The point \(\bar x\) is epsilon-subgradient stationary when
\[
0\in\partial_{\varepsilon}f(\bar x),
\qquad
\partial_{\varepsilon}f(\bar x):=\{v:f(y)\ge f(\bar x)+\langle v,y-\bar x\rangle-\varepsilon\ \text{for all }y\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
For \(v=0\), this predicate states that no point has objective value more than \(\varepsilon\) below \(f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex point is epsilon-subgradient stationary when zero is an epsilon-subgradient, equivalently when its value is within epsilon of the infimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Epsilon-Strong Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-max outer composite model with epsilon-active pieces and an epsilon-bounded pulled-back residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The point \(\bar x\) is composite epsilon-strongly stationary if there exists \(\lambda\in\Delta_m\) such that \(\lambda_i=0\) for every \(i\notin I_{\varepsilon}(F(\bar x))\) and
\[
\left\|F'(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\nabla h_i(F(\bar x))\right\|\le\varepsilon.
\]
The weights, epsilon-active indices, and residual jointly form the certificate and preserve the composite finite-max structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite epsilon-strong stationarity uses weights on nearly active outer pieces and bounds the norm of their Jacobian-pulled weighted gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), and \(h(z)=\max_{1\le i\le m}h_i(z)\) with continuously differentiable \(h_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left\|F'(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\sum_i\lambda_i\nabla h_i(F(\bar x))\right\|\le\varepsilon\) with \(\operatorname{supp}(\lambda)\subseteq I_{\varepsilon}(F(\bar x))\).

notation.meaning: Outer pieces within epsilon of the active maximum.

children.title: Pointwise Subdifferential Distance
children.top_down_role: Distance evaluated using the subdifferential at the candidate point.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, with \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\).
\(\partial f\) denotes the limiting subdifferential and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(\bar x):=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(\bar x))\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise residual based on the finite-dimensional limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The pointwise subdifferential-distance certificate at \(\bar x\) is
\[
r(\bar x):=\inf\{\|v\|:v\in\partial f(\bar x)\}.
\]
The reported point is epsilon-stationary in this sense when \(r(\bar x)\le\varepsilon\), equivalently when some \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\) satisfies \(\|v\|\le\varepsilon\). The convention assigns \(r(\bar x)=+\infty\) if \(\partial f(\bar x)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This certificate measures the smallest norm of a limiting subgradient at the reported point and requires that norm not exceed epsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Subdifferential Distance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise limiting-subdifferential residual is precise and fits the certificate leaf, but no authoritative source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Nearby-Point Subdifferential Distance
children.top_down_role: Distance evaluated at a controlled displacement from the reported point.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and \(\partial f\) is its limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\delta}(\bar x):=\inf_{\|y-\bar x\|\le\delta}\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Allowed displacement from the reported point.
Best subdifferential residual over the closed displacement ball.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-subdifferential residual evaluated at an existentially chosen point in a closed displacement ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nearby-point subdifferential distance at \(\bar x\) and radius \(\delta\) is
\[
r_{\delta}(\bar x):=\inf_{\|y-\bar x\|\le\delta}\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y)).
\]
An epsilon certificate is \(r_{\delta}(\bar x)\le\varepsilon\). Equivalently up to attainment, one exhibits a point \(y\) with \(\|y-\bar x\|\le\delta\) and a limiting subgradient \(v\in\partial f(y)\) whose norm is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual is the best subdifferential distance obtainable at a point lying within delta of the reported point.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-Point Subdifferential Distance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The infimum-based residual is well defined, but `r_delta(bar x) <= epsilon` need not yield a witness attaining both non-strict bounds unless attainment is established. The exact convention and any attainment claim require a source.

children.title: Enlarged-Subdifferential Distance
children.top_down_role: Distance measured using neighborhood or tolerance enlargements.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and \(\partial f\) is its limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial^{[\delta]}f(\bar x))\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Closed convex neighborhood enlargement of the limiting subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood convexification enlargement; other literature may use value-aware or graph-based enlargements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the neighborhood-enlarged subdifferential by
\[
\partial^{[\delta]}f(\bar x):=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{y\in\mathbb{B}_{\delta}(\bar x)}\partial f(y)\right).
\]
The enlarged-subdifferential distance certificate with tolerances \((\varepsilon,\delta)\) is
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial^{[\delta]}f(\bar x))\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus a vector of norm at most \(\varepsilon\) must be representable as a limit of convex combinations of subgradients sampled within distance \(\delta\) of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This certificate measures distance to the closed convex hull of subgradients collected throughout a delta-neighborhood of the point.
knowledge_statements.title: Enlarged-Subdifferential Distance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record explicitly defines a coherent neighborhood convexification, but enlarged-subdifferential conventions vary materially. No source supports this particular construction as the intended leaf concept.

children.title: Epsilon–Delta Near-Stationarity

knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon–Delta Near-Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-tolerance limiting-subdifferential certificate separating displacement from residual size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The reported point \(\bar x\) is epsilon-delta near-stationary if there exist \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(v\in\partial f(y)\) satisfying
\[
\|y-\bar x\|\le\delta
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\|v\|\le\varepsilon.
\]
The witness \((y,v)\) separately certifies geometric proximity to \(\bar x\) and stationarity quality at \(y\). When \(\delta=0\), the condition reduces to pointwise subdifferential-distance stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearby point within delta must possess a limiting subgradient whose norm is at most epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and \(\partial f\) is its limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists y,v:\ \|y-\bar x\|\le\delta,\ v\in\partial f(y),\ \|v\|\le\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variational Principle for Near-Minimizers and Small Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative displacement and stationarity guarantee for near-minimizers of lower-semicontinuous functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} be lower semicontinuous with \inf f\in\mathbb{R}. If \varepsilon>0 and f(\bar x)\leq\inf f+\varepsilon, then for every \delta>0 there exist \widetilde x\in\mathbb{R}^n and \widetilde v\in\partial f(\widetilde x) such that \|\widetilde x-\bar x\|\leq\varepsilon/\delta,\ f(\widetilde x)\leq f(\bar x),\ \text{and}\ \|\widetilde v\|\leq\delta.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every epsilon-near-minimizer lies within epsilon divided by delta of a point with no larger objective value and a subgradient of norm at most delta.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\widetilde x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \widetilde v\in\partial f(\widetilde x):\ \|\widetilde x-\bar x\|\leq\varepsilon/\delta,\ f(\widetilde x)\leq f(\bar x),\ \|\widetilde v\|\leq\delta.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and \(\partial f\) is its limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial(f-\langle p,\cdot\rangle)(y)\) for some \(\|p\|\le\varepsilon\) and \(\|y-\bar x\|\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact limiting stationarity of a nearby point for a norm-controlled linear perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A perturbed-problem stationarity certificate for \(\bar x\) is a pair \((y,p)\) such that
\[
\|y-\bar x\|\le\delta,
\qquad
\|p\|\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
0\in\partial f_p(y),
\]
where \(f_p(z)=f(z)-\langle p,z\rangle\). For the limiting subdifferential, the last inclusion is equivalent to \(p\in\partial f(y)\); hence exact stationarity of the controlled perturbation certifies epsilon-delta near-stationarity for the original objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearby point is exactly stationary after adding a linear perturbation whose coefficient has norm at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbed-Problem Stationarity

children.title: Proximal Near-Point Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Nearby criticality obtained at a proximal or envelope point.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
\(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), with the upper bound omitted when \(\rho=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\) and \(g=(x-y)/\lambda\in\partial f(y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weakly convex finite-dimensional objective and a single-valued proximal point below the weak-convexity threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a reported point \(x\), let
\[
y=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x),
\qquad
g=\frac{x-y}{\lambda}.
\]
Proximal optimality gives \(g\in\partial f(y)\). Consequently, bounds \(\|g\|\le\varepsilon\) and \(\|x-y\|\le\delta\) form a proximal near-point stationarity certificate. Since \(\|x-y\|=\lambda\|g\|\), the residual bound alone guarantees displacement at most \(\lambda\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal point carries a subgradient equal to the scaled displacement, so one vector controls both nearby displacement and stationarity quality.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Near-Point Stationarity

children.title: Goldstein Subdifferential Certificates
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood convexification certificates for Lipschitz objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Goldstein Subdifferential Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Clarke–Goldstein certificate for a locally Lipschitz objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\overline B(x,\delta)\), where \(\delta\ge 0\), and define
\[\partial_\delta^G f(x):=\operatorname{conv}\!\bigcup_{y\in\overline B(x,\delta)}\partial^C f(y).\]
The Goldstein certificate is the minimum-norm vector
\[g_\delta(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{g\in\partial_\delta^G f(x)}\|g\|.\]
For any \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the inequality \(\|g_\delta(x)\|\le\varepsilon\), equivalently \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_\delta^G f(x))\le\varepsilon\), certifies that zero is within residual \(\varepsilon\) of the convexified Clarke subgradients generated in the radius-\(\delta\) neighborhood of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum-norm convex combination of Clarke subgradients sampled within radius delta certifies Goldstein stationarity when its norm is at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|g_\delta(x)\|\le\varepsilon\iff\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_\delta^G f(x))\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Clarke subdifferential of f at y

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional definition of the Goldstein subdifferential and its minimum-norm certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically coherent and correctly typed, but the precise Goldstein-subdifferential convention requires an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Epsilon–Delta Goldstein Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Goldstein certificates with separate neighborhood and residual tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon–Delta Goldstein Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates the stationarity residual \(\varepsilon\) from the neighborhood radius \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\overline B(x,\delta)\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon,\delta\ge0\), the point \(x\) is called \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-Goldstein stationary when
\[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial_\delta^G f(x)\right)\le\varepsilon,\qquad \partial_\delta^G f(x)=\operatorname{conv}\!\bigcup_{y\in\overline B(x,\delta)}\partial^C f(y).\]
Thus \(\delta\) controls spatial enlargement and \(\varepsilon\) controls the residual. The cases \(\varepsilon=0\) and \(\delta=0\) respectively give exact neighborhood stationarity and ordinary \(\varepsilon\)-Clarke stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is epsilon–delta Goldstein stationary when zero lies within epsilon of the convexified Clarke subgradients from its delta-neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ is }(\varepsilon,\delta)\text{-Goldstein stationary}\iff\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_\delta^G f(x))\le\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional two-tolerance Goldstein stationarity definition

children.title: Goldstein Descent-or-Certificate Principles
children.top_down_role: Alternatives between neighborhood descent and approximate stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Goldstein Descent-or-Certificate Principles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection separates a Goldstein stationarity certificate from a common neighborhood descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=\partial_\delta^G f(x)\) and let \(g=\operatorname{proj}_G(0)\). For every \(\varepsilon\ge0\), exactly one of the following alternatives applies: \(\|g\|\le\varepsilon\), which is an \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-Goldstein certificate; or \(\|g\|>\varepsilon\), in which case \(d=-g/\|g\|\) satisfies
\[\langle v,d\rangle\le-\|g\|<-\varepsilon\qquad\text{for every }v\in G.\]
Consequently, for every \(y\in\overline B(x,\delta)\),
\[f^\circ(y;d)=\max_{v\in\partial^C f(y)}\langle v,d\rangle\le-\|g\|,\]
so \(d\) is a common strict Clarke-descent direction throughout the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum-norm Goldstein subgradient is either small enough to certify stationarity or determines a direction having uniformly negative Clarke directional derivative throughout the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|g\|\le\varepsilon\), or \(d=-g/\|g\|\) obeys \(f^\circ(y;d)\le-\|g\|<-\varepsilon\) for every \(y\in\overline B(x,\delta)\).

notation.meaning: minimum-norm element of the Goldstein subdifferential

children.title: Ekeland Perturbation Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Ekeland Perturbation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete-metric Ekeland certificate with its finite-dimensional subdifferential consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,d)\) be complete and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below. If \(f(\bar x)\le\inf_X f+\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon>0\), then for every \(\lambda>0\) there exists \(y\in X\) such that
\[d(y,\bar x)\le\lambda,\qquad f(y)\le f(\bar x),\qquad f(y)<f(z)+(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(z,y)\quad(z\ne y).\]
Thus \(y\) exactly minimizes \(z\mapsto f(z)+(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(z,y)\). If \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), this yields the verifiable criticality certificate
\[0\in\partial f(y)+(\varepsilon/\lambda)\overline B,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\le\varepsilon/\lambda.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-minimizer admits a point within lambda that exactly minimizes a Lipschitz perturbation and has subdifferential residual at most epsilon divided by lambda.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(y,\bar x)\le\lambda\) and, in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\le\varepsilon/\lambda\).

notation.meaning: limiting subdifferential in the finite-dimensional consequence

children.title: Approximate Extremal Principles

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Extremal Principles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional approximate Fréchet-normal certificate for a locally extremal finite set system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let closed sets \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_m\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) share \(\bar x\), and suppose they are locally extremal there: some neighborhood \(U\) admits vectors \(a_{ik}\to0\) with \(\bigcap_{i=1}^m(\Omega_i-a_{ik})\cap U=\varnothing\) for every \(k\). Then, for every \(\eta>0\), there exist \(x_i\in\Omega_i\cap B(\bar x,\eta)\) and Fréchet normals \(x_i^*\in\widehat N_{\Omega_i}(x_i)\) satisfying
\[\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i^*\|=1,\qquad \left\|\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*\right\|<\eta.\]
The normalization excludes the zero tuple, while the second inequality supplies approximate separation or stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally extremal finite family of closed sets has nearby nontrivial Fréchet normals whose normalized sum is arbitrarily small.
assumptions_latex: The family is locally extremal at \(\bar x\) under vanishing translations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x_i,x_i^*:\ \|x_i-\bar x\|<\eta,\ x_i^*\in\widehat N_{\Omega_i}(x_i),\ \sum_i\|x_i^*\|=1,\ \|\sum_i x_i^*\|<\eta\).

children.title: Fuzzy Subdifferential Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Fuzzy Subdifferential Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional fuzzy sum certificate assembled from subgradients at separate nearby points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\), finite at \(\bar x\), with one function locally Lipschitz there. If \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f_1+f_2\), then for every \(\eta>0\) there exist \(x_i\in B(\bar x,\eta)\) and limiting subgradients \(v_i\in\partial f_i(x_i)\) such that
\[|f_i(x_i)-f_i(\bar x)|<\eta\quad(i=1,2),\qquad \|v_1+v_2\|<\eta.\]
Hence the nearby data \((x_1,v_1,x_2,v_2)\) form an approximate stationarity certificate even when an exact same-point subdifferential sum rule is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local minimum of a sum yields subgradients at nearby points whose sum is arbitrarily small, with both points and function values controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(f_1,f_2\) are lower semicontinuous and finite at \(\bar x\).
One of \(f_1,f_2\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f_1+f_2\).

children.title: Pointwise-to-Nearby Transfer

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise-to-Nearby Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers a pointwise residual certificate to the nearby-point format without loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be a set-valued stationarity mapping between normed spaces. A pointwise \(\varepsilon\)-certificate at \(x\) is a vector \(v\in D(x)\) with \(\|v\|\le\varepsilon\). For every displacement tolerance \(\delta\ge0\), choosing \(y=x\) gives
\[\|y-x\|=0\le\delta,\qquad v\in D(y),\qquad \|v\|\le\varepsilon.\]
Thus every pointwise \(\varepsilon\)-certificate is also a nearby \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-certificate, with neither residual inflation nor actual displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any pointwise certificate is automatically a nearby certificate by selecting the nearby point equal to the original point.
assumptions_latex: \(D:X\rightrightarrows Y\) is a set-valued stationarity mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=x\) satisfies \(\|y-x\|\le\delta\), \(v\in D(y)\), and \(\|v\|\le\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: immediate inclusion of pointwise certificates in the nearby-point certificate format
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Nearby-to-Pointwise Recovery
children.top_down_role: Conditions supporting recovery of a reported-point certificate from a nearby witness.

knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-to-Pointwise Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers a pointwise residual using an outer-continuity modulus of the stationarity mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:X\rightrightarrows Y\) have nonempty values, and suppose that near \(x\)
\[D(y)\subset D(x)+\omega(\|y-x\|)\overline B_Y,\]
where \(\omega:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is nondecreasing and \(\omega(0)=0\). If a nearby certificate satisfies \(\|y-x\|\le\delta\), \(v\in D(y)\), and \(\|v\|\le\varepsilon\), then some \(u\in D(x)\) obeys
\[\|u\|\le\varepsilon+\omega(\delta).\]
Consequently, \(\operatorname{dist}(0,D(x))\le\varepsilon+\omega(\delta)\); recovery is exact in the limit whenever \(\omega(\delta)\to0\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer continuity of the stationarity mapping converts a nearby residual epsilon into a pointwise residual bounded by epsilon plus the continuity modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,D(x))\le\varepsilon+\omega(\delta)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct residual estimate under one-sided Hausdorff continuity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Displacement Tolerance Costs
children.top_down_role: Losses attributable to moving between reported points and neighboring certificate locations.

knowledge_statements.title: Displacement Tolerance Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies residual inflation caused by moving a certificate between nearby base points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:X\rightrightarrows Y\) have nonempty closed values and be Hausdorff-Lipschitz on a set \(U\):
\[d_H(D(x),D(y))\le L\|x-y\|\qquad(x,y\in U).\]
Define \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,D(x))\). Then
\[|r(x)-r(y)|\le L\|x-y\|.\]
Accordingly, a certificate at \(y\) with \(\|y-x\|\le\delta\) and residual at most \(\varepsilon\) yields a pointwise residual at \(x\) of at most \(\varepsilon+L\delta\). The additive term \(L\delta\) is the displacement tolerance cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Hausdorff-Lipschitz stationarity mapping, moving a certificate by delta can increase its residual by at most L delta.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\operatorname{dist}(0,D(x))-\operatorname{dist}(0,D(y))|\le L\|x-y\|\le L\delta\).

notation.meaning: Hausdorff distance between nonempty closed sets

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distance to a fixed point is Lipschitz with respect to Hausdorff distance

children.title: Neighborhood-to-Subdifferential Transfer
children.top_down_role: Passage from neighborhood-based generalized-gradient certificates to subdifferential certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood-to-Subdifferential Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents a finite-dimensional Goldstein certificate using finitely many nearby Clarke subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\overline B(x,\delta)\). Every \(g\in\partial_\delta^G f(x)\) admits, by Carathéodory's theorem, a representation
\[g=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_i v_i,\qquad m\le n+1,\qquad \alpha_i\ge0,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_i=1,\]
with \(y_i\in\overline B(x,\delta)\) and \(v_i\in\partial^C f(y_i)\). Hence a neighborhood certificate \(\|g\|\le\varepsilon\) transfers to a finite collection of nearby pointwise subdifferential data whose convex combination has residual at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every Goldstein certificate in n dimensions can be represented by at most n plus one Clarke subgradients taken at nearby points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_i v_i\) for some \(m\le n+1\), \(y_i\in\overline B(x,\delta)\), and \(v_i\in\partial^C f(y_i)\).

notation.meaning: Clarke subgradients at the nearby points

children.title: Subdifferential-to-Neighborhood Enlargement
children.top_down_role: Passage from subdifferential information to enlarged neighborhood certificate sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential-to-Neighborhood Enlargement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone embedding of pointwise Clarke certificates into every Goldstein enlargement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\overline B(x,\delta)\). Since \(x\in\overline B(x,\delta)\),
\[\partial^C f(x)\subseteq\partial_\delta^G f(x).\]
Moreover, if \(0\le\delta_1\le\delta_2\), then
\[\partial_{\delta_1}^G f(x)\subseteq\partial_{\delta_2}^G f(x),\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_{\delta_2}^G f(x))\le\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_{\delta_1}^G f(x)).\]
Thus every pointwise Clarke \(\varepsilon\)-certificate remains valid after neighborhood enlargement, while enlarging the radius can only decrease the Goldstein stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise Clarke subdifferential lies in every Goldstein enlargement, and increasing the neighborhood radius cannot increase the stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial^C f(x)\subseteq\partial_{\delta_1}^G f(x)\subseteq\partial_{\delta_2}^G f(x)\) and the corresponding distances to zero are nonincreasing.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: immediate set inclusion and monotonicity from the Goldstein definition
