children.title: Conversion Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural settings where neighborhood enlargement introduces no essential certificate gap.

knowledge_statements.title: Conversion Exactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies zero-radius, locally stable, and vanishing-radius exactness of Goldstein conversion within a fixed locally Lipschitz neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz on an open neighborhood of \(\overline B(x,r)\) for some \(r>0\). Then
\[\partial_0^G f(x)=\partial^C f(x).\]
For a fixed \(\delta\in(0,r]\), equality also holds whenever \(\partial^C f(y)\subseteq\partial^C f(x)\) for every \(y\in\overline B(x,\delta)\). Moreover,
\[\bigcap_{0<\delta\le r}\partial_\delta^G f(x)=\partial^C f(x),\qquad \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_\delta^G f(x))=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial^C f(x)).\]
Thus neighborhood-to-pointwise conversion is exact at zero radius, under local subdifferential stability, and asymptotically as the radius vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a fixed neighborhood on which the function is locally Lipschitz, Goldstein and Clarke certificates agree at radius zero, under local subdifferential stability, and asymptotically as the radius tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz on an open neighborhood of \(\overline B(x,r)\) for some \(r>0\).
For fixed-radius equality, \(0<\delta\le r\) and \(\partial^C f(y)\subseteq\partial^C f(x)\) for every \(y\in\overline B(x,\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_0^G f(x)=\partial^C f(x)\), \(\bigcap_{0<\delta\le r}\partial_\delta^G f(x)=\partial^C f(x)\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_\delta^G f(x))\to\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial^C f(x))\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: radius of a fixed neighborhood on which local Lipschitzness holds
monotone convergence of the neighborhood radius to zero

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested compact convex-set convergence using outer semicontinuity and local boundedness of the finite-dimensional Clarke subdifferential

children.title: Certificate Conversion Degradation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degradation occurring when translating between approximate certificate languages.

children.title: Conversion Tolerance Degradation
children.top_down_role: Accuracy losses incurred when translating between approximate certificate languages.

assumptions_latex: Two certificate residuals \(R_A,R_B:X\to[0,\infty]\) vanish exactly at their respective stationary points.
A conversion estimate \(R_B(x)\leq \phi(R_A(x))\) holds on a specified class, where \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is nondecreasing and \(\phi(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_A(x)\leq\varepsilon\Longrightarrow R_B(x)\leq\phi(\varepsilon)\); the conversion degrades tolerance when \(\phi(\varepsilon)>\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Residuals measuring source and target certificate violations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract residual-based formulation; the node path does not identify a particular pair of approximate certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_A\) and \(R_B\) be nonnegative certificate residuals and suppose \(R_B(x)\leq\phi(R_A(x))\), with \(\phi\) nondecreasing and \(\phi(0)=0\). Then every \(\varepsilon\)-certificate of type \(A\), meaning \(R_A(x)\leq\varepsilon\), yields a \(\phi(\varepsilon)\)-certificate of type \(B\). The conversion has tolerance degradation at \(\varepsilon\) precisely when \(\phi(\varepsilon)>\varepsilon\); common degradation laws include \(\phi(t)=ct\) with \(c>1\) and \(\phi(t)=ct^\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A source residual at most epsilon produces a target residual at most phi(epsilon); conversion degrades tolerance wherever phi(epsilon) exceeds epsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Conversion Tolerance Degradation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract residual implication is mathematically coherent and fits the degradation leaf, but no source is supplied for this formulation or for the asserted common degradation laws. The intended certificate pair and applicable problem class also remain unspecified.

children.title: Dimension-Dependent Conversion Constants
children.top_down_role: Conversion quality governed by constants that deteriorate with ambient dimension.

assumptions_latex: For every dimension \(n\), residuals \(R_{A,n},R_{B,n}\) are defined on a common class \(X_n\).
There are constants \(c_n>0\) such that \(R_{B,n}(x)\leq c_nR_{A,n}(x)\) for all \(x\in X_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{A,n}(x)\leq\varepsilon\Longrightarrow R_{B,n}(x)\leq c_n\varepsilon\), with dimension-dependent degradation when \(\sup_n c_n=\infty\).

notation.meaning: Source and target residuals in dimension n.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract linear conversion regime; no particular certificate pair or dimension scaling is fixed by the path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear conversion between certificate families in dimension \(n\) has constant \(c_n\) when \(R_{B,n}(x)\leq c_nR_{A,n}(x)\) for every admissible \(x\in X_n\). Consequently, \(R_{A,n}(x)\leq\varepsilon\) implies \(R_{B,n}(x)\leq c_n\varepsilon\). The conversion constants are genuinely dimension-dependent when no uniform constant works, equivalently when the least valid constants satisfy \(\sup_{n\geq1}c_n=\infty\). Any asserted rate such as \(c_n=O(\sqrt n)\) requires the specific norms and certificate definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dimension-n conversion multiplies tolerance by c_n. It is genuinely dimension-dependent when the smallest valid constants are unbounded as dimension grows.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Conversion Constants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The characterization using least valid constants is coherent and fits the dimension-dependent leaf, but the record has no citation and identifies no concrete certificate families, norms, or dimension scaling supported by evidence.

children.title: Dimension-Free Conversion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structures supporting certificate conversions without dimension-driven degradation.

assumptions_latex: For each \(n\), residuals \(R_{A,n},R_{B,n}\) are defined using fixed, consistently normalized norms.
A constant \(c<\infty\), independent of \(n\), satisfies \(R_{B,n}(x)\leq cR_{A,n}(x)\) for every admissible \(n\) and \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{A,n}(x)\leq\varepsilon\Longrightarrow R_{B,n}(x)\leq c\varepsilon\) uniformly in \(n\).

notation.meaning: Dimension-indexed source and target certificate residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform residual conversion across finite dimensions, conditional on consistent norm normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate conversion is dimension-free on the family \((X_n)_{n\geq1}\) if there exists \(c<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that \(R_{B,n}(x)\leq cR_{A,n}(x)\) for every \(n\geq1\) and every \(x\in X_n\). Thus an \(\varepsilon\)-certificate of type \(A\) always converts to a \(c\varepsilon\)-certificate of type \(B\), without deterioration as \(n\) increases. Dimension-freeness is meaningful only after fixing the norm and residual normalizations across dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conversion is dimension-free when one finite constant converts source residuals to target residuals uniformly over all dimensions under fixed norm normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Free Conversion Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform-constant formulation correctly expresses a dimension-free conversion regime once normalizations are fixed, but no source supports the formulation or establishes such a regime for any specified certificate pair.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clarke-normal stationarity requires cancellation between a Clarke objective subgradient and a Clarke feasible-set normal, both convexified generalized derivatives.

children.title: Normal Fritz John Regime
children.top_down_role: Fritz John certificates with an active objective multiplier.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Fritz John Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Clarke–Fritz John certificate with a positive objective multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) locally minimize a locally Lipschitz function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) subject to locally Lipschitz inequalities \(g_i(x)\le 0\), indexed by \(i=1,\ldots,m\). A normal Fritz John certificate consists of multipliers \(\lambda_0>0\) and \(\lambda_i\ge 0\), not all zero, such that \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\) for every \(i\) and \[0\in \lambda_0\partial^C f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x).\] Dividing all multipliers by \(\lambda_0\) gives the normalized KKT form with objective multiplier equal to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive objective multiplier makes the homogeneous Fritz John system rescalable to a nonsmooth KKT system with objective multiplier one.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is a feasible local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_0>0\) permits normalization to \(0\in\partial^C f(\bar x)+\sum_i(\lambda_i/\lambda_0)\partial^C g_i(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Abnormal Fritz John Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Fritz John certificate whose objective multiplier vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For locally Lipschitz inequality constraints \(g_i(x)\le 0\), an abnormal Fritz John certificate at a feasible point \(\bar x\) consists of multipliers \(\lambda_0=0\) and \(\lambda_i\ge 0\), with \((\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)\ne 0\), satisfying \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\) and \[0\in\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x).\] The stationarity relation contains no objective subgradient and therefore cannot be normalized to an objective multiplier equal to one; it certifies degeneracy of the active constraint geometry rather than objective-sensitive KKT stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An abnormal certificate has zero objective multiplier and a nonzero combination of active constraint subgradients containing zero.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are locally Lipschitz near the feasible point \(\bar x\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\sum_i\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x)\) with \(\lambda\ne0\), so KKT normalization is impossible.

children.title: Directional Constraint Qualifications

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Constraint Qualifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke–Mangasarian–Fromovitz directional qualification for locally Lipschitz inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\), where each \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz, and let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). The directional Clarke constraint qualification holds at a feasible point \(\bar x\) if there exists \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \[g_i^{\circ}(\bar x;d)<0\qquad\text{for every }i\in I(\bar x).\] Equivalently, every active constraint has strictly negative Clarke directional derivative along one common direction. This excludes any nonzero vector \(\lambda\ge0\), supported on \(I(\bar x)\), for which \(0\in\sum_i\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One direction must strictly decrease every active constraint in the Clarke directional sense, thereby excluding nonzero abnormal inequality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\) for every \(i\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\lambda\ge0\) with \(\lambda\ne0\), \(\lambda_i=0\) off \(I(\bar x)\), and \(0\in\sum_i\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The directional qualification and exclusion of abnormal multipliers are plausible and appropriately scoped, but no citation supports the stated implication or its precise Clarke formulation.

children.title: Metric-Regularity Constraint Qualifications
children.top_down_role: Covering and error-bound regularity supporting multiplier normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Regularity Constraint Qualifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric regularity of a set-valued constraint mapping near its reference graph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^q\) have locally closed graph, and suppose \(\bar y\in F(\bar x)\). Metric regularity of the constraint system at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) means that there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\), and \(\kappa>0\), such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(y))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(y,F(x))\qquad(x,y)\in U\times V.\] This error-bound inequality supplies quantitative local solvability and rules out the corresponding nonzero singular coderivative multiplier under the standard finite-dimensional coderivative criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric regularity bounds distance to a perturbed feasible set by constraint residual, providing local solvability and excluding singular multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is locally closed near \((\bar x,\bar y)\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(y))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(y,F(x))\) locally around \((\bar x,\bar y)\).

children.title: Normal-Cone Calculus Qualifications

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Calculus Qualifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic limiting-normal qualification for an intersection of closed sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C,D\subset\mathbb R^n\) be locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\cap D\). The basic normal-cone qualification is \[N_C(\bar x)\cap\bigl(-N_D(\bar x)\bigr)=\{0\}.\] Under this qualification, limiting normals obey the intersection calculus inclusion \[N_{C\cap D}(\bar x)\subset N_C(\bar x)+N_D(\bar x).\] Thus a normal to the feasible intersection can be decomposed into component normals. Equality may require additional regularity, such as convexity or suitable normal regularity, and is not asserted by the basic qualification alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the component sets have no opposing nonzero limiting normals, every limiting normal to their intersection decomposes into component normals.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(D\) are locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\cap D\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{C\cap D}(\bar x)\subset N_C(\bar x)+N_D(\bar x)\).

children.title: Multiplier Normalization Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Regularity routes converting abnormal multiplier certificates into normalized multiplier systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Normalization Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-objective normalization of homogeneous Fritz John multiplier systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a homogeneous stationarity certificate has multipliers \((\lambda_0,\lambda)\ne(0,0)\), with \(\lambda_0>0\), and satisfies \[0\in\lambda_0\partial f(\bar x)+\mathcal G(\bar x,\lambda),\] where \(\mathcal G(\bar x,t\lambda)=t\mathcal G(\bar x,\lambda)\) for every \(t>0\), and all sign and complementarity conditions are positively homogeneous. Setting \(\mu=\lambda/\lambda_0\) and dividing the certificate by \(\lambda_0\) yields \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\mathcal G(\bar x,\mu).\] Hence normalization is valid exactly for certificates whose objective multiplier is positive; no analogous division is available when \(\lambda_0=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive homogeneity lets any Fritz John certificate with positive objective multiplier be rescaled uniquely to objective multiplier one.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G(\bar x,t\lambda)=t\mathcal G(\bar x,\lambda)\) for every \(t>0\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu=\lambda/\lambda_0\) satisfies \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\mathcal G(\bar x,\mu)\).

children.title: Normalization Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degenerate settings where abnormal multipliers persist or normalization cannot be justified.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth one-dimensional example forcing an abnormal Fritz John certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad x^2\le0.\] The feasible set is \(\{0\}\), so \(\bar x=0\) is a global minimizer. Fritz John stationarity requires nonnegative multipliers \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1)\ne(0,0)\) satisfying \[0=\lambda_0 f'(0)+\lambda_1 g'(0)=\lambda_0.\] Consequently \(\lambda_0=0\) and necessarily \(\lambda_1>0\). Every certificate is abnormal and cannot be divided by its objective multiplier. The failure occurs because the sole active constraint has zero gradient at the feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimizing x subject to x²≤0, the only feasible point is optimal, but every Fritz John certificate has zero objective multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every nonzero Fritz John multiplier pair satisfies \(\lambda_0=0\) and \(\lambda_1>0\), so normalization fails.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example is mathematically coherent and the counterexample kind fits the failure-regime leaf, but the record supplies no evidence source for this nontrivial example.

children.title: Nonsmooth KKT Conditions
children.top_down_role: Normalized multiplier stationarity families for nonsmooth constrained problems.

children.title: Convex Nonsmooth KKT
children.top_down_role: Convex multiplier certificates and their sufficiency role.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Nonsmooth KKT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex inequality program under Slater’s condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper convex functions, and suppose there is \(x^s\in\operatorname{dom}f\) with \(g_i(x^s)<0\) for all \(i\). A feasible point \(\bar x\) minimizes \(f\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\) if and only if there exist \(\lambda_i\ge0\) such that \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial g_i(\bar x),\qquad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\quad(i=1,,m).\] Thus the convex KKT system is both necessary and sufficient under Slater’s condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under convexity and Slater’s condition, feasibility plus subgradient stationarity, nonnegative multipliers, and complementary slackness exactly characterize global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are proper convex functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is globally optimal if and only if the displayed convex KKT multipliers exist.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the necessary-and-sufficient theorem. With extended-valued convex functions, the stated Slater hypothesis may not by itself provide the domain regularity needed for the subdifferential sum and KKT necessity; the displayed index also contains the typo “i=1,,m”.

children.title: Clarke KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: KKT-type certificate systems formulated with Clarke generalized derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Clarke KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke-subdifferential KKT certificate for locally Lipschitz inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For locally Lipschitz functions \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), a Clarke KKT certificate at a feasible point \(\bar x\) is a vector \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfying \[0\in\partial^C f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x),\qquad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] The inclusion is interpreted as existence of subgradients \(v_0\in\partial^C f(\bar x)\) and \(v_i\in\partial^C g_i(\bar x)\) such that \(v_0+\sum_i\lambda_i v_i=0\). It is a necessary local-optimality certificate only under an appropriate constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Clarke KKT certificate combines objective and active-constraint Clarke subgradients using nonnegative complementary multipliers to obtain zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are locally Lipschitz near the feasible point \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial^C f(\bar x)+\sum_i\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x)\) with \(\lambda\ge0\) and complementary slackness.

knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Multiplier Existence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of normalized Clarke multipliers under a strict common descent qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) locally minimize a locally Lipschitz function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) subject to locally Lipschitz inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\). If there exists \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(g_i^{\circ}(\bar x;d)<0\) for every active index \(i\in I(\bar x)\), then there are multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\) satisfying \[0\in\partial^C f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x),\qquad \lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0.\] Thus the objective multiplier in the associated Fritz John system can be chosen equal to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer, strict common descent for all active constraints guarantees normalized Clarke KKT multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is a feasible local minimizer.
There exists \(d\) with \(g_i^{\circ}(\bar x;d)<0\) for every \(i\in I(\bar x)\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying Clarke stationarity and \(\lambda_i g_i(\bar x)=0\) for every \(i\).

children.title: Abnormal Clarke Multiplier Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Degenerate regimes producing abnormal or noninformative Clarke multiplier certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Abnormal Clarke Multiplier Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of normalized Clarke multipliers when active constraints admit an abnormal dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For locally Lipschitz inequalities, the normalization boundary is reached when there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\), supported on \(I(\bar x)\), such that \[0\in\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial^C g_i(\bar x).\] This is an abnormal Clarke multiplier system: its objective multiplier is zero. The condition negates the no-abnormal-multiplier qualification and prevents Fritz John theory alone from guaranteeing a normalized Clarke KKT certificate. In particular, for \(g(x)=x^2\le0\) at \(\bar x=0\), every \(\lambda>0\) satisfies \(0=\lambda g'(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero positive dependence among active Clarke subgradients marks the boundary where Fritz John multipliers may remain abnormal and unnormalizable.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are locally Lipschitz near the feasible point \(\bar x\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonzero abnormal constraint multiplier exists, so normalized Clarke KKT existence is not ensured.

knowledge_statements.title: Mordukhovich Stationarity Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-subdifferential certificate for a nonsmooth geometric constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous and let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be locally closed at a feasible point \(\bar x\). The Mordukhovich stationarity condition is \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_\Omega(\bar x),\] where both objects are limiting constructions. For a constraint representation \(\Omega=\{x:F(x)\in Q\}\), a multiplier form is obtained when some \(y^*\in N_Q(F(\bar x))\) satisfies \[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+D^*F(\bar x)(y^*).\] Valid necessity and the coderivative normal formula require the corresponding limiting-calculus qualification.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\) and finite at \(\bar x\).\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_\Omega(\bar x)\), with the displayed coderivative multiplier form when applicable.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Exact-Penalty Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex affine-composite correspondence between KKT certificates and stationary points of a distance penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex, let \(D\subset\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(c(x)=Ax-b\), and let \(\rho\geq0\). Using the Euclidean distance and norm, define \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(c(x),D)\). For every feasible point \(\bar x\),
\[0\in\partial P_\rho(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y\in N_D(c(\bar x)):\ 0\in\partial f(\bar x)+A^{\mathsf T}y,\ \|y\|\leq\rho.\]
Consequently, a constrained KKT certificate with multiplier \(y\) yields penalized stationarity whenever \(\rho\geq\|y\|\), while every feasible stationary point of \(P_\rho\) yields a constrained KKT multiplier bounded by \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective and affine convex-set constraint, feasible distance-penalty stationarity is equivalent to KKT stationarity with a multiplier whose Euclidean norm does not exceed the nonnegative penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper convex and finite near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial P_\rho(\bar x)\iff\exists y\in N_D(c(\bar x)):0\in\partial f(\bar x)+A^{\mathsf T}y,\ \|y\|\leq\rho\).

children.title: Pull-Out Penalization Certificates
children.top_down_role: Structure-preserving penalty certificates for composite constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Pull-Out Penalization Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-like certificate obtained by pulling a distance subgradient through a smooth composite constraint map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\rho>0\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz, let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(D\subset\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty and closed. Define \(P_\rho=f+\rho\operatorname{dist}(c(\cdot),D)\), and let \(\partial\) denote the limiting subdifferential. Suppose that at \(\bar x\) the exact sum and composite rules give
\[\partial P_\rho(\bar x)=\partial f(\bar x)+\rho\nabla c(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\partial\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,D)(c(\bar x)).\]
A pull-out certificate is a pair \((u,v)\) satisfying
\[u\in\partial f(\bar x),\qquad v\in\partial\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,D)(c(\bar x)),\qquad u+\rho\nabla c(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}v=0.\]
Such a pair certifies \(0\in\partial P_\rho(\bar x)\). At a feasible point, the additional relations \(v\in N_D(c(\bar x))\) and \(\|v\|\leq1\) may be checked as part of the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an explicitly assumed exact limiting-subdifferential sum and chain rule, an objective subgradient and a pulled-out distance subgradient certify penalized stationarity through one adjoint-Jacobian equation.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho>0\), \(f\) is locally Lipschitz, and \(c\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
The displayed exact limiting-subdifferential sum and composite rule holds at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u+\rho\nabla c(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}v=0\Longrightarrow0\in\partial P_\rho(\bar x)\).

Suppose \((\bar x,\bar y)\in X\times\mathbb R^k\) is a B-stationary point of (9.31) for some \(\rho>0\). If there exists \(dy\in\mathbb R^k\) such that \(H_j'(\bar y;dy)<0\) for every \(j\) with \(H_j(\bar y)>0\), \(H_j'(\bar y;dy)\leq0\) for every \(j\) with \(H_j(\bar y)=0\), and, for every \(i\), \(dy_i<0\), \(dy_i>0\), or \(dy_i=0\) according as \(\bar y_i>G_i(\bar x)\), \(\bar y_i<G_i(\bar x)\), or \(\bar y_i=G_i(\bar x)\), then \(\bar x\) is a B-stationary solution of (9.29).

children.title: Penalty–Stationarity Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Spurious or weakened penalized criticality outside exactness regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty–Stationarity Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A subthreshold penalty both loses feasible stationarity and creates an infeasible stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\) subject to \(x=0\), and use the penalty \(P_\rho(x)=(x-1)^2+\rho|x|\). The only feasible point \(\bar x=0\) is a constrained local minimizer and hence constrained-stationary. If \(0<\rho<2\), then
\[0\notin\partial P_\rho(0)=-2+\rho[-1,1],\]
so constrained stationarity does not transfer to the penalty. Moreover, \(x_\rho=1-\rho/2>0\) satisfies \(P_\rho'(x_\rho)=0\) but violates \(x=0\). Thus a penalty parameter below the multiplier threshold can simultaneously remove the desired stationary point and introduce spurious infeasible criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the exactness threshold, an equality penalty can reject the constrained solution and possess a different, infeasible stationary point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\notin\partial P_\rho(0)\) while \(0=P_\rho'(1-\rho/2)\) and \(1-\rho/2\neq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak, S-, M-, and C-Stationarity for the MPCC Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-based MPCC stationarity definitions at a feasible point arising from the convex lower-level bilevel formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y,\bar\lambda)$ be feasible for the MPCC. It is weakly stationary if there exist $w\in\mathbb R^m$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^r$ such that, with derivatives evaluated at $(\bar x,\bar y)$,
\[
0=\nabla_xF-\nabla^2_{yx}f\,w-\nabla^2_{yx}(\bar\lambda^Tg)\,w+\nabla_xg^T\xi,
\]
\[
0=\nabla_yF-\nabla^2_{yy}f\,w-\nabla^2_{yy}(\bar\lambda^Tg)\,w+\nabla_yg^T\xi,
\]
\[
\xi_i=0\quad\text{if }g_i(\bar x,\bar y)<0\text{ and }\bar\lambda_i=0,
\]
and
\[
\nabla_yg_i(\bar x,\bar y)^Tw=0\quad\text{if }g_i(\bar x,\bar y)=0\text{ and }\bar\lambda_i>0.
\]
For every index satisfying $g_i(\bar x,\bar y)=\bar\lambda_i=0$, it is respectively S-, M-, or C-stationary if, in addition,
\[
\xi_i\geq0,\qquad \nabla_yg_i(\bar x,\bar y)^Tw\leq0;
\]
\[
\bigl(\xi_i>0\text{ and }\nabla_yg_i(\bar x,\bar y)^Tw<0\bigr)\quad\text{or}\quad \xi_i\nabla_yg_i(\bar x,\bar y)^Tw=0;
\]
\[
\xi_i\nabla_yg_i(\bar x,\bar y)^Tw\leq0,
\]
respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak stationarity requires the two multiplier balance equations and the stated conditions on inactive and positive-multiplier active indices. At biactive indices, the three additional conditions define S-, M-, and C-stationarity, respectively.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y,\bar\lambda)\text{ is feasible for the MPCC}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\bar x,\bar y,\bar\lambda)\text{ has the specified weak, S-, M-, or C-stationarity property exactly when the corresponding multiplier conditions hold.}

knowledge_statements.title: Weak MPCC Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier stationarity imposing no sign relation on biactive complementarity multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an MPCC with \(g(x)\leq0\), \(h(x)=0\), \(G(x)\geq0\), \(H(x)\geq0\), and \(G_i(x)H_i(x)=0\). A feasible point \( ar x\) is weakly stationary if multipliers \((\lambda,\eta,
u,\xi)\) exist such that
\[0=
abla f( ar x)+\sum_j\lambda_j
abla g_j( ar x)+\sum_k\eta_k
abla h_k( ar x)-\sum_i
u_i
abla G_i( ar x)-\sum_i\xi_i
abla H_i( ar x),\]
with \(\lambda\geq0\), \(\lambda_jg_j( ar x)=0\), \(
u_i=0\) on \(I^{+0}\), and \(\xi_i=0\) on \(I^{0+}\). On \(I^{00}\), both \(
u_i\) and \(\xi_i\) are unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak MPCC stationarity requires the multiplier balance and ordinary inequality complementarity, but leaves both biactive multipliers unrestricted.

knowledge_statements.title: Clarke MPCC Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak MPCC stationarity strengthened by the Clarke sign-product condition at biactive indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the smooth MPCC and index sets \(I^{+0}\), \(I^{0+}\), and \(I^{00}\), a feasible point \(\bar x\) is Clarke-stationary if it possesses weak-stationarity multipliers \((\lambda,\eta,\nu,\xi)\) and, for every biactive index, satisfies
\[\nu_i\xi_i\geq0\qquad(i\in I^{00}).\]
Thus the two multipliers at a biactive complementarity pair must have compatible signs or one must vanish. No additional restriction is imposed on the multiplier that corresponds to the locally active equality branch at indices in \(I^{+0}\) or \(I^{0+}\), beyond the zero-multiplier rules already contained in weak stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clarke MPCC stationarity is weak stationarity plus a nonnegative product condition for each pair of biactive multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The point \(\bar x\) is feasible for a continuously differentiable MPCC.
The weak-stationarity equations and zero-multiplier rules hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu_i\xi_i\geq0\) for every \(i\in I^{00}\).

notation.meaning: multipliers of the two complementarity components

knowledge_statements.title: Weak–Clarke Strictness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical biactive example showing that weak stationarity need not imply Clarke stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x,y)=x-y\) and impose the single complementarity pair \(x\geq0\), \(y\geq0\), and \(xy=0\). At \((0,0)\), both components are biactive. With the stationarity convention
\[0=
abla f(0,0)-
u(1,0)-\xi(0,1),\]
the unique multipliers are \(
u=1\) and \(\xi=-1\). They satisfy weak MPCC stationarity because biactive multipliers are unrestricted. However, \(
u\xi=-1<0\), so no Clarke-stationarity multiplier exists. Thus this MPCC has a weakly stationary point that is not Clarke-stationary, proving that Clarke stationarity is strictly stronger than weak stationarity in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The example has a unique opposite-signed biactive multiplier pair, so its origin is weakly stationary but not Clarke-stationary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0)\) is weakly stationary but not Clarke-stationary.

knowledge_statements.title: Bouligand MPCC Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal directional stationarity over the Bouligand tangent cone to the MPCC feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\) be the feasible set of the continuously differentiable MPCC with constraints \(g(x)\leq0\), \(h(x)=0\), \(G(x)\geq0\), \(H(x)\geq0\), and \(G_i(x)H_i(x)=0\) for every complementarity index \(i\). At a feasible point \(\bar x\), define the Bouligand tangent cone by
\[T_\Omega(\bar x)=\left\{d:\exists t_k\downarrow0,\ \exists d_k\to d\text{ with }\bar x+t_kd_k\in\Omega\text{ for every }k\right\}.\]
The point \(\bar x\) is Bouligand MPCC-stationary if
\[\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}d\geq0\qquad\text{for every }d\in T_\Omega(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bouligand MPCC stationarity excludes every first-order descent direction in the contingent tangent cone to the actual MPCC feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The MPCC data are continuously differentiable near the feasible point \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}d\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_\Omega(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Strong–Bouligand Coincidence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of strong multiplier stationarity and primal Bouligand stationarity under MPCC-LICQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible point \(\bar x\), suppose MPCC-LICQ holds: the gradients of all equalities, active ordinary inequalities, \(G_i\) for \(i\in I^{0+}\cup I^{00}\), and \(H_i\) for \(i\in I^{+0}\cup I^{00}\) are linearly independent. Then \(\bar x\) is Bouligand MPCC-stationary if and only if it is strongly MPCC-stationary. Under this hypothesis the multiplier system is unique, and polarity of the MPCC linearized cone forces the biactive multipliers to satisfy \(\nu_i\geq0\) and \(\xi_i\geq0\). Thus the primal directional certificate and the strong multiplier certificate describe the same stationary points in the MPCC-LICQ regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MPCC-LICQ, Bouligand directional stationarity and strong multiplier stationarity are equivalent, with unique multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is feasible for a continuously differentiable MPCC.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\text{ is B-stationary}\iff\bar x\text{ is S-stationary}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Strong–Bouligand Separation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate complementarity mapping separates primal Bouligand stationarity from strong multiplier stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the one-dimensional MPCC minimizing \(f(x)=x\) subject to \(G(x)=x^2\geq0\), \(H(x)=x^2\geq0\), and \(G(x)H(x)=0\). Its feasible set is the singleton \(\{0\}\); hence its tangent cone at \(0\) is \(\{0\}\), and \(0\) is Bouligand-stationary. However, \(G'(0)=H'(0)=0\), so every strong-stationarity multiplier equation reduces to
\[0=f'(0)-\nu G'(0)-\xi H'(0)=1,\]
which is impossible. Thus Bouligand stationarity need not imply strong stationarity when the complementarity gradients are degenerate and an MPCC constraint qualification fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With vanishing complementarity gradients, an isolated feasible point is Bouligand-stationary although no strong multiplier equation can hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=0\) is Bouligand-stationary but not strongly stationary.

knowledge_statements.title: Abstract MPEC Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coderivative multiplier certificate for equilibrium constraints represented by a generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Psi:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) have locally closed graph, and consider minimizing a locally Lipschitz function \(\varphi\) over \(\Omega=\{z:0\in\Psi(z)\}\). Define
\[D^*\Psi(\bar z,0)(\lambda)=\{z^*:(z^*,-\lambda)\in N_{\operatorname{gph}\Psi}(\bar z,0)\}.\]
An abstract limiting MPEC-stationarity certificate at a feasible point \(\bar z\) is a pair \((v,\lambda)\) satisfying
\[v\in\partial\varphi(\bar z),\qquad -v\in D^*\Psi(\bar z,0)(\lambda).\]
If a local minimizer \(\bar z\) satisfies a qualification yielding \(N_\Omega(\bar z)\subset\bigcup_\lambda D^*\Psi(\bar z,0)(\lambda)\), then such a certificate necessarily exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Abstract MPEC stationarity balances an objective subgradient with a coderivative image of an equilibrium multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The stated inverse-image normal-cone qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(v,\lambda):v\in\partial\varphi(\bar z),\ -v\in D^*\Psi(\bar z,0)(\lambda)\).

notation.meaning: limiting coderivative of the equilibrium mapping
limiting normal cone to the graph

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent MPEC Stationarity Tests under SBCQ and Full CQ
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence among MPEC stationarity, dual-cone membership, linearized minimization, and a distance-penalty inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose SBCQ holds at \( ar z\in\mathcal F\) and the full CQ holds, so that \(\mathcal L( ar z;\mathcal F)=\mathcal T( ar z;\mathcal F)\). Then the following are equivalent: (a) \( ar z\) is stationary; (b) \(
abla f( ar z)^Tdz\ge 0\) for every \(dz\in\mathcal L( ar z;\mathcal F)\), equivalently \(
abla f( ar z)\in\mathcal L( ar z;\mathcal F)^*\); (c) \(dz=0\) is an optimal solution of \(\min\{
abla f( ar z)^Tdz:dz\in\mathcal L( ar z;\mathcal F)\}\); and (d) for every \(\alpha\ge\|
abla f( ar z)\|\) and every \(dz\in\mathbb R^{n+m}\), \[
abla f( ar z)^Tdz+\alpha\operatorname{dist} igl(dz,\mathcal L( ar z;\mathcal F) igr)\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under SBCQ and equality of the MPEC tangent and full linearized cones, stationarity is equivalent to nonnegative directional derivative on the linearized cone, membership of the gradient in its positive dual cone, optimality of the zero direction for the linearized problem, and the stated distance-penalty inequality for every sufficiently large penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal L(\bar z;\mathcal F)=\mathcal T(\bar z;\mathcal F)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (a)\Longleftrightarrow(b)\Longleftrightarrow(c)\Longleftrightarrow(d).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upper-subdifferential necessary condition for an abstract MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coderivative-normal necessary condition for a local solution of an abstract equilibrium-constrained problem in Asplund spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local solution of the abstract MPEC. Assume that $X$ and $Y$ are Asplund spaces, $\operatorname{gph}S$ is locally closed around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\Omega$ is locally closed around $\bar x$, either $S$ is PSNC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$ or $\Omega$ is SNC at $\bar x$, and
\[
D_M^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(0)\cap\bigl(-N(\bar x;\Omega)\bigr)=\{0\}.
\]
Then, for every $(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)$,
\[
-x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local abstract-MPEC solution, the stated Asplund-space, local-closedness, compactness, and mixed qualification assumptions imply the coderivative-normal inclusion for every upper regular subgradient of the objective.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local solution of the abstract MPEC}
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed around }(\bar x,\bar y)
S\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)\ \lor\ \Omega\text{ is SNC at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\quad -x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized linear-independence qualification implies S-stationarity for an MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: S-stationarity condition for the MPEC reformulation of a bilevel program with a convex lower-level problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\bar x,\bar y)\) be a local minimizer of \((\mathrm{MPEC})\) satisfying MSCQ, and define \(P(x,y):=(y,-\nabla_y f(x,y))\). If
\[
\nabla P(\bar x,\bar y)\mathbb R^{n+m}+\mathcal L\!\left(T_{\operatorname{gph}N_\Gamma}(P(\bar x,\bar y))\right)=\mathbb R^{2m},
\]
where \(\mathcal L\) denotes the generalized linearity space, then \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is S-stationary for \((\mathrm{MPEC})\): there exists \(w\) such that
\[
0=\nabla_xF(\bar x,\bar y)+\nabla_{xy}^2f(\bar x,\bar y)w,
\]
\[
0\in\nabla_yF(\bar x,\bar y)+\nabla_{yy}^2f(\bar x,\bar y)w+\widehat D N_\Gamma\!\left(\bar y,-\nabla_yf(\bar x,\bar y)\right)(w).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an MSCQ local minimizer, the stated generalized linear-independence condition for the mapping P and the tangent cone to the graph of the lower-level normal-cone mapping guarantees S-stationarity and the displayed stationarity system.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local minimizer of }(\mathrm{MPEC})
\nabla P(\bar x,\bar y)\mathbb R^{n+m}+\mathcal L\!\left(T_{\operatorname{gph}N_\Gamma}(P(\bar x,\bar y))\right)=\mathbb R^{2m}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is S-stationary for }(\mathrm{MPEC})\text{ and admits }w\text{ satisfying the displayed system.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonqualified multiplier conditions for an abstract MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fritz John-type upper- and lower-subdifferential necessary conditions without the mixed MPEC qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local solution of the abstract MPEC. Assume that $X,Y$ are Asplund spaces, $\operatorname{gph}S$ is locally closed around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, and $\Omega$ is locally closed around $\bar x$. If either $S$ is PSNC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$ or $\Omega$ is SNC at $\bar x$, then there exists $\lambda\in\{0,1\}$ such that, for every $(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)$, there exist
\[
x_1^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(\lambda y^*),\qquad x_2^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega)
\]
satisfying
\[
\lambda x^*+x_1^*+x_2^*=0,
\qquad (\lambda,x_1^*)\ne(0,0).
\]
If, in addition, $\varphi$ is locally Lipschitz around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, then there exist $\lambda\geq0$, $(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)$, $x_1^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(\lambda y^*)$, and $x_2^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega)$ satisfying the same equation and nontriviality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without the mixed qualification, a local abstract-MPEC solution still satisfies a nontrivial Fritz John-type coderivative-normal condition. One multiplier in {0,1} works for all upper regular subgradients; if the objective is locally Lipschitz, an existential limiting-subgradient version holds with a nonnegative multiplier.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MSCQ Implies M-Stationarity for an Abstract MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A necessary optimality condition for an equilibrium constraint represented by a normal-cone generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local optimal solution of the MPEC and define
\[
\Sigma(\alpha):=\{(x,y)\mid \alpha\in\nabla_y f(x,y)+N_\Gamma(y)\}.
\]
If $\Sigma$ is calm (pseudo upper-Lipschitz continuous) at $(0,\bar x,\bar y)$, that is, MSCQ holds at $(\bar x,\bar y)$, then $(\bar x,\bar y)$ is M-stationary: there exists $w\in\mathbb R^m$ such that
\[
0=\nabla_xF(\bar x,\bar y)+\nabla^2_{yx}f(\bar x,\bar y)w,
\]
and
\[
0\in\nabla_yF(\bar x,\bar y)+\nabla^2_{yy}f(\bar x,\bar y)w+D^*N_\Gamma\bigl(\bar y,-\nabla_yf(\bar x,\bar y)\bigr)(w).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local MPEC solution, calmness of the perturbed generalized-equation solution map, identified here with MSCQ, guarantees M-stationarity through the stated gradient equation and coderivative inclusion.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local optimal solution of the MPEC}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Abstract MPEC conditions under a Lipschitz-like equilibrium mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper- and lower-subdifferential stationarity conditions obtained from Lipschitz-like regularity of the equilibrium mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local solution of the abstract MPEC in Asplund spaces $X,Y$. Suppose $\operatorname{gph}S$ is locally closed around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\Omega$ is locally closed around $\bar x$, and $S$ is Lipschitz-like around $(\bar x,\bar y)$. Then
\[
\forall(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\qquad -x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega).
\]
If, in addition, $\varphi$ is locally Lipschitz around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, then
\[
\exists(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\qquad -x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a local abstract-MPEC solution, a Lipschitz-like equilibrium mapping gives the coderivative-normal inclusion for every upper regular subgradient. If the objective is also locally Lipschitz, the inclusion holds for some limiting subgradient.

\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed around }(\bar x,\bar y)
S\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent cone and stationarity under BIF
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the feasible tangent cone and first-order stationarity of an MPEC whose local equilibrium response satisfies BIF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be convex and let $(\bar x,\bar y)\in\mathcal F$. Under BIF, $$\mathcal T((\bar x,\bar y);\mathcal F)=\{(d_x,d_y)\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X)\times\mathbb R^m:d_y=y'(\bar x;d_x)\}.$$ Consequently, $(\bar x,\bar y)$ is stationary if and only if, for every $d_x\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X)$, $$\nabla_x f(\bar x,\bar y)^Td_x+\nabla_y f(\bar x,\bar y)^Ty'(\bar x;d_x)\ge 0.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the upper-level set is convex and the equilibrium response satisfies BIF, each feasible tangent direction is exactly a parameter tangent direction paired with the directional derivative of the implicit response. The point is stationary if and only if the induced objective directional derivative is nonnegative for every parameter tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal T((\bar x,\bar y);\mathcal F)=\{(d_x,y'(\bar x;d_x)):d_x\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X)\},\quad (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ stationary}\iff \forall d_x\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X),\;\nabla_x f^Td_x+\nabla_y f^Ty'(\bar x;d_x)\ge0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower-subdifferential necessary conditions for an abstract MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two alternative qualification regimes yielding a limiting-subdifferential coderivative-normal stationarity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local solution of the abstract MPEC. Assume that $X,Y$ are Asplund spaces, $\varphi$ is lower semicontinuous around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\operatorname{gph}S$ is locally closed around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, and $\Omega$ is locally closed around $\bar x$. Then
\[
\exists(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y):\quad 0\in x^*+D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega)
\]
under either of these regimes: (i) all assumptions of the upper-subdifferential condition hold, $\varphi$ is SNEC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$, and
\[
(x_\infty^*,y_\infty^*)\in\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\quad 0\in x_\infty^*+D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y_\infty^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega)
\]
imply $x_\infty^*=y_\infty^*=0$; these additional assumptions hold automatically if $\varphi$ is locally Lipschitz around $(\bar x,\bar y)$. (ii) $S$ is SNC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\Omega$ is SNC at $\bar x$, and
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(x_\infty^*,y_\infty^*)\in\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\quad x_1^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y_\infty^*),\\
&x_2^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega),\quad x_\infty^*+x_1^*+x_2^*=0
\end{aligned}
\]
imply $x_\infty^*=y_\infty^*=x_1^*=x_2^*=0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local abstract-MPEC solution satisfies a limiting-subdifferential coderivative-normal stationarity condition under either the upper-condition hypotheses plus SNEC and a singular-subgradient qualification, or SNC of both constraint objects plus the stronger decomposition qualification.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local solution of the abstract MPEC}
\varphi\text{ is lower semicontinuous around }(\bar x,\bar y)
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed around }(\bar x,\bar y)
\text{Either qualification regime (i) or qualification regime (ii) stated above holds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)\quad 0\in x^*+D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega).

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Normal-Cone Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-tolerance certificate separating distance to the constraint set from normal-cone criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. For \(\delta\geq0\), define the enlarged normal cone \(N_C^{\delta}(x)=\bigcup\{N_C(y):y\in C,\ \|y-x\|\leq\delta\}\). A point \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-normal-cone stationary if \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\delta\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)+N_C^{\delta}(x))\leq\varepsilon\). When \(x\in C\) and \(\delta=0\), this reduces to the exact-cone residual \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)+N_C(x))\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate separately bounds infeasibility and the distance of zero from the objective subdifferential plus an exact or locally enlarged constraint normal cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\delta\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)+N_C^{\delta}(x))\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Optimality Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic Fritz–John certificate that remains meaningful without a pointwise constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the locally Lipschitz program \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\) and \(h(x)=0\), a feasible point \(\bar x\) has a sequential Fritz–John certificate if there exist \(x^k\to\bar x\), scalars \(\alpha_k\geq0\), multipliers \(\lambda^k\geq0\), \(\mu^k\), and corresponding limiting subgradients such that \(\alpha_k+\|\lambda^k\|+\|\mu^k\|=1\), the Lagrangian stationarity residual tends to zero, \(\|[g(x^k)]_+\|+\|h(x^k)\|\to0\), and \(\lambda_i^k g_i(x^k)\to0\) for every \(i\). A KKT-type sequence additionally has \(\alpha_k\to1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential certificate uses nearby points and normalized Fritz–John multipliers whose stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity residuals vanish; no pointwise constraint qualification is built into its definition.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are locally Lipschitz near the feasible point \(\bar x\).
The stationarity residual uses compatible selections from their limiting subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity residuals converge to zero along a normalized multiplier sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility–Stationarity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate tolerances prevent one residual scale from concealing poor feasibility or poor criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_f(x)\geq0\) measure constraint violation and \(r_s(x)\geq0\) measure stationarity. An \((\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_s)\)-certificate requires \(r_f(x)\leq\varepsilon_f\) and \(r_s(x)\leq\varepsilon_s\). For weights \(a,b>0\), the scalar bound \(a r_f(x)+b r_s(x)\leq\varepsilon\) implies only \(r_f(x)\leq\varepsilon/a\) and \(r_s(x)\leq\varepsilon/b\). Conversely, the two componentwise bounds imply \(a r_f(x)+b r_s(x)\leq a\varepsilon_f+b\varepsilon_s\). Thus changing weights changes the certified tradeoff unless an additional error-bound relation links the residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility and stationarity should be reported separately: a weighted aggregate controls them only at weight-dependent accuracies unless an error bound couples the two residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a r_f+b r_s\leq\varepsilon\Rightarrow(r_f\leq\varepsilon/a,\ r_s\leq\varepsilon/b)\), while componentwise bounds imply the corresponding weighted bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Moreau-Envelope Gradient-Norm Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weakly convex finite-dimensional stationarity measured by the gradient of a differentiable Moreau envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and choose \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), with \(1/0=+\infty\). Define \(f_\lambda(x)=\min_y\{f(y)+\|y-x\|^2/(2\lambda)\}\). The proximal minimizer \(P_\lambda(x)\) is unique, \(f_\lambda\) is continuously differentiable, and \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\). Hence \(x\) has an \(\varepsilon\)-Moreau-envelope certificate precisely when \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weakly convex function and a valid smoothing parameter, the Moreau envelope is smooth; its gradient norm is the scaled displacement to the unique proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|=\lambda^{-1}\|x-P_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard differentiability formula for the Moreau envelope of a weakly convex function

children.title: Proximal-Point Displacement Certificate
children.top_down_role: Stationarity measured by displacement from a point to its proximal image.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Point Displacement Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent weakly convex stationarity certificate expressed as unscaled distance to the proximal image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the weak-convexity and parameter assumptions ensuring that \(P_\lambda(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y\{f(y)+\|y-x\|^2/(2\lambda)\}\) is single-valued, define the displacement \(d_\lambda(x)=\|x-P_\lambda(x)\|\). A point \(x\) has an \(\eta\)-proximal-displacement certificate when \(d_\lambda(x)\leq\eta\). Since \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\), this certificate is exactly equivalent to the Moreau-envelope bound \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\eta/\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal displacement and Moreau-envelope gradient norm carry the same information, differing only by the parameter factor λ.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_\lambda(x)\leq\eta\iff\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\eta/\lambda\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: immediate scaling identity between proximal displacement and envelope gradient

children.title: Envelope-to-Near-Point Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Conversion from envelope stationarity to subdifferential stationarity at a proximal point.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-to-Near-Point Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope criticality transfers to limiting-subdifferential criticality at the associated nearby proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, let \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), and set \(y=P_\lambda(x)\). Proximal optimality and weak convexity give \(v=\lambda^{-1}(x-y)=\nabla f_\lambda(x)\in\partial f(y)\). Consequently, if \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\), then \(\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon\). Thus envelope stationarity at \(x\) certifies ordinary limiting-subdifferential stationarity at a quantitatively nearby point \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small envelope gradient produces a proximal point within λε whose limiting subdifferential contains a vector of norm at most ε.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\Rightarrow\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal optimality inclusion and Moreau-gradient identity for weakly convex functions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly targets transfer to a nearby proximal point, but the proximal optimality inclusion and limiting-subdifferential conclusion lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Proximal-Point Residual Certificates

children.title: Exact Proximal-Point Residual Certificate
children.top_down_role: Residual criticality based on an exact proximal point.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Proximal-Point Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation yields a computable residual and a subgradient at the proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, with \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). For \(y=P_\lambda(x)\), define the exact proximal residual \(r_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-y)\). Then \(r_\lambda(x)\in\partial f(y)\), so \(\|r_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\). Moreover, \(r_\lambda(x)=0\) if and only if \(x=y\) and \(0\in\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled displacement to an exact proximal point is a subgradient there; its norm certifies nearby stationarity and vanishes exactly at a stationary fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\lambda(x)\in\partial f(P_\lambda(x))\), with \(r_\lambda(x)=0\iff0\in\partial f(x)\).

children.title: Inexact Proximal Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates separating proximal-subproblem error from outer stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-component certificate separating inner proximal optimality error from outer displacement residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and take \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). An inexact proximal certificate at \(x\) consists of \(y\), an error \(e\), and the outer residual \(r=\lambda^{-1}(x-y)\), such that \(e\in\partial f(y)+(y-x)/\lambda\), \(\|e\|\leq\eta\), and \(\|r\|\leq\varepsilon\). The inclusion gives \(r+e\in\partial f(y)\); hence \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon+\eta\) and \(\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact proximal certificate records inner-solve error and outer displacement separately; together they bound subdifferential stationarity at the computed proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon+\eta\) and \(\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\).

children.title: Resolvent-Fixed-Point Residual Pair

children.title: Resolvent Residuals
children.top_down_role: Operator-resolvent representations of proximal stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone-inclusion residual obtained by evaluating the resolvent of a maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\) be maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space and let \(\lambda>0\). Its resolvent \(J_{\lambda A}=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}\) is single-valued, and the scaled resolvent residual is \(R_{\lambda A}(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-J_{\lambda A}x)\). By the resolvent definition, \(R_{\lambda A}(x)\in A(J_{\lambda A}x)\). Therefore \(\|R_{\lambda A}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an element of \(A\) with norm at most \(\varepsilon\) at the nearby point \(J_{\lambda A}x\), and \(R_{\lambda A}(x)=0\) exactly when \(0\in A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled resolvent displacement belongs to the operator at the resolvent point, and it vanishes exactly at solutions of the monotone inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\lambda A}(x)\in A(J_{\lambda A}x)\) and \(R_{\lambda A}(x)=0\iff0\in A(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining identity of the resolvent of a maximal monotone operator
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates measuring failure of a proximal or resolvent fixed-point relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unscaled residual certifying approximate fixed points of the resolvent and solutions of the associated inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\) be maximal monotone, let \(\lambda>0\), and define the fixed-point residual \(F_{\lambda A}(x)=x-J_{\lambda A}x\). A bound \(\|F_{\lambda A}(x)\|\leq\eta\) certifies that \(x\) is an \(\eta\)-approximate fixed point of the resolvent. Exactly, \(F_{\lambda A}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x=J_{\lambda A}x\), which is equivalent to \(0\in A(x)\). The scaled resolvent residual satisfies \(R_{\lambda A}(x)=\lambda^{-1}F_{\lambda A}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The distance from a point to its resolvent image is a fixed-point residual; zero residual is equivalent to solving the monotone inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\lambda A}(x)=0\iff x=J_{\lambda A}x\iff0\in A(x)\), and \(R_{\lambda A}=\lambda^{-1}F_{\lambda A}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic fixed-point characterization of resolvent zeros
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Residual Scaling Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes governing comparability between resolvent and fixed-point residual magnitudes.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\lambda(x)=\lambda\nabla f_\lambda(x)\), so \(\|r_\lambda(x)\|=\lambda\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\) and either residual vanishes exactly when the other does.

notation.meaning: Proximal mapping of f with parameter lambda.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean weakly convex Moreau envelopes in the single-valued proximal regime.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), strong convexity of the proximal subproblem makes \(P_\lambda(x)\) single-valued, and the Moreau envelope is continuously differentiable with \[\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}\bigl(x-P_\lambda(x)\bigr)=\lambda^{-1}r_\lambda(x).\] Consequently, the resolvent fixed-point residual and the envelope-gradient residual contain identical stationarity information, differing only by the positive scale factor \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal fixed-point residual equals the envelope gradient multiplied by the proximal parameter, so both residuals detect exactly the same stationary points.

children.title: Structured Proximal Residuals
children.top_down_role: Proximal certificate families adapted to composite, constrained, and model-based structures.

children.title: Prox-Linear Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Model-gradient and proximal residuals for composite objectives.

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=h(c(x))+g(x)\), where \(h\) is proper closed convex, \(c\) is continuously differentiable, and \(g\) is proper closed convex.
The displayed prox-linear subproblem has a minimizer for the chosen \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_t(x)=0\) exactly when \(0\in \nabla c(x)^\top\partial h(c(x))+\partial g(x)\), subject to the convex-composite subdifferential chain rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-composite Euclidean prox-linear stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[d_t(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{h\bigl(c(x)+\nabla c(x)d\bigr)+g(x+d)+\frac{1}{2t}\|d\|^2\right\},\qquad G_t(x)=-t^{-1}d_t(x).\] The vector \(G_t(x)\) is a verifiable prox-linear residual. In particular, \(G_t(x)=0\) if and only if \[0\in \nabla c(x)^\top\partial h(c(x))+\partial g(x),\] whenever the standard convex-composite chain rule is valid at \(x\). Thus a zero residual certifies first-order stationarity of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled prox-linear step is a stationarity residual; it vanishes exactly when the convex-composite first-order inclusion holds under the chain rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Residual Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate has the correct local role and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source is supplied for the precise prox-linear subproblem, the zero-residual equivalence, or the required convex-composite chain-rule qualification.

children.title: Model-Based Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Stationarity measures produced by local approximation models.

assumptions_latex: For each base point \(x\), \(m_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and satisfies \(m_x(x)=f(x)\).
For \(t>0\), the regularized model subproblem has a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable quantity \(R_t(x)=t^{-1}(x-T_t(x))\) is zero exactly when \(x\) minimizes its regularized local model; under first-order model consistency, this certifies stationarity of \(f\).

notation.meaning: Local approximation model of f at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic proximal regularization of a first-order consistent local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \[T_t(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{m_x(y)+\frac{1}{2t}\|y-x\|^2\right\},\qquad R_t(x)=t^{-1}\bigl(x-T_t(x)\bigr).\] Then \(R_t(x)=0\) if and only if the selected regularized model point equals its base point. If the model is first-order consistent in the sense that \(\partial m_x(x)=\partial f(x)\) for the chosen subdifferential, this equality yields \(0\in\partial f(x)\). Hence \(R_t(x)\) is a directly checkable model-based stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled displacement from the base point to a regularized model minimizer is a residual; zero certifies stationarity when model and objective subdifferentials agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Based Residual Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic model residual fits the leaf, but the phrase 'chosen subdifferential' does not identify a calculus with a valid Fermat rule, and no source supports the asserted first-order consistency implication. The mathematical version therefore depends on unresolved model and subdifferential choices.

children.title: Convex-Set Constrained Proximal Residuals
children.top_down_role: Proximal certificates after incorporating a convex feasible-set indicator.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(\lambda>0\).
At the point under consideration, the convex subdifferential sum rule gives \(\partial(f+\delta_C)(x)=\partial f(x)+N_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in C\), \(R_{\lambda,C}(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\partial f(x)+N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Indicator of the feasible set C.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex objectives over closed convex feasible sets represented through indicator functions.

source_refs.locator: 6.1.1 The convex constrained case p. 324

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), define \[P_{\lambda,C}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\},\qquad R_{\lambda,C}(x)=\lambda^{-1}\bigl(x-P_{\lambda,C}(x)\bigr).\] For every \(x\in C\), the constrained proximal residual satisfies \[R_{\lambda,C}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial f(x)+N_C(x),\] provided the stated convex subdifferential sum rule holds at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex objective over a closed convex set, the constrained proximal residual vanishes exactly when the convex subgradient and normal-cone stationarity inclusion holds, subject to the stated sum rule.

children.title: Weak-Convexity Applicability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing the validity and interpretation of envelope and proximal certificates.

children.title: Envelope-Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter ranges supporting a single-valued proximal map and smooth-envelope interpretation.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict regime \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\) guarantees a single-valued proximal map and a continuously differentiable Moreau envelope with \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uniform parameter regime implied solely by the weak-convexity modulus.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The envelope parameter must satisfy \[0<\lambda<\frac{1}{\rho},\] where \(1/0=+\infty\). In this regime, the function \(y\mapsto f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\) is strongly convex for every \(x\), so \(P_\lambda(x)\) is uniquely defined. Moreover, \(f_\lambda\) is continuously differentiable and \[\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}\bigl(x-P_\lambda(x)\bigr).\] At or beyond \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), weak convexity alone does not ensure either uniqueness or this smooth-envelope representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rho-weakly convex function, parameters strictly below 1/rho guarantee a unique proximal point and the smooth Moreau-envelope gradient formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Parameter Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

children.title: Proximal-Map Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Failure of single-valued proximal certificate representations outside valid regimes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(0)=\mathbb{R}\), so the proximal map is not single-valued at the boundary parameter.

notation.meaning: Proximal objective at base point x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional boundary example showing sharp loss of proximal uniqueness.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex because \(f(y)+(\rho/2)y^2=0\). At \(x=0\) and \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), its proximal objective is \[q_0(y)=-\frac{\rho}{2}y^2+\frac{1}{2\lambda}y^2=0\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}.\] Hence every \(y\in\mathbb{R}\) minimizes the subproblem, and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(0)=\mathbb{R}\). A single-valued residual or envelope-gradient representation therefore cannot be inferred at the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At lambda equal to 1/rho, a negative quadratic has every real number as a proximal point at zero, destroying residual uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Map Nonuniqueness

children.title: Stationary but Nonoptimal Weakly Convex Points
children.top_down_role: Limits of proximal and envelope stationarity as an optimality guarantee.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial f(0)\) and \(\nabla f_\lambda(0)=0\), although \(0\) is neither a local nor a global minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth one-dimensional example separating weakly convex stationarity from optimality.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is \(2\)-weakly convex and satisfies \(f'(0)=0\). For \(0<\lambda<1/2\), the proximal objective at zero is \[f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}y^2=\left(\frac{1}{2\lambda}-1\right)y^2,\] whose unique minimizer is \(P_\lambda(0)=0\). Thus \(\nabla f_\lambda(0)=\lambda^{-1}(0-P_\lambda(0))=0\). Nevertheless, \(f(y)<f(0)\) for every \(y\ne0\), so zero is a strict local maximum rather than a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weakly convex function minus x squared has zero proximal and envelope residual at zero, but zero is a strict maximum, not a minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationary but Nonoptimal Weakly Convex Points
